findings.title: Entire retention loop (review schedule, strength, completion flags, pre-test) lives only in localStorage; the one server write fails silently
findings.evidence: handleComplete writes revvy_complete_* (line 197), revvy_review_schedule (lines 200-210) and strength (recordReview, line 214) to localStorage only. The sole server call, saveLearnModeProgress (lines 224-235), POSTs to app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js which upserts last_result: 'correct' / 'complete' / `post:${n}` (route.js lines 40, 59) into practice_question_progress.last_result, declared BOOLEAN in scripts/create-practice-progress-table.sql:13. The route never checks the upsert error and returns { ok: true }; the client .catch(() => {}) swallows everything. GET /api/learn-mode/progress is referenced by no component (grep of app/components/lib found only the route itself). StudyApp.jsx:308-316 builds learnModeCompletions by scanning localStorage; ReviewMode.jsx:8-15 reads the schedule from localStorage.
findings.studentImpact: A student who completes a topic on their school laptop and opens Revvy on their phone (or in incognito, or after Safari's 7-day ITP storage eviction, or after clearing site data) has: no completion dot in the sidebar, no strength bar, no scheduled reviews, no pre-test record, and the section re-opens at the DB-saved step with the pre-test gate suppressed only because isResuming is true. The 1/3/7/14-day spaced review promise is broken for anyone who is not on the exact same browser profile every time. Logged-in status changes nothing.
findings.fix: Persist completion, review schedule and strength server-side keyed by user_id (a small user_section_state table: completed_at, review_interval_idx, next_due, reviews, quiz_accuracy, pretest_score, pretest_questions). Fix or delete /api/learn-mode/progress: either change last_result to TEXT or stop writing strings; check the upsert error and return 500 so the failure is visible. Hydrate localStorage from the server on login as a cache, not the source of truth.

findings.title: Nothing ever brings a student back for a due review; the only 'review due' banner is hidden on the screens a returning student actually lands on
findings.evidence: The due-review banner (lines 289-296) is rendered inside the step view, which is reached only after the early returns for the pre-test gate (line 249) and the completion screen (line 259). A completed section therefore never shows the banner. HomeScreen's 'Overdue' stat and 'Review N overdue cards' recommendation come from /api/progress/dashboard (route.js lines 148-153), which counts practice_question_progress rows with next_review < now, i.e. flashcard/practice rows, not the learn-mode schedule. No email, push, service worker, cron or reminder code exists (grep for resend/sendgrid/nodemailer/web-push/cron/reminder across app, components, lib returned nothing; no vercel.json crons).
findings.studentImpact: Day 1 after completing 'introductory-concepts', a student re-opens the app. Every section change lands on the Learn tab; if they open the section they finished, they see the Completion screen (no banner). If they open a new section they first hit the pre-test gate (no banner). Only once they are inside the step view of an unfinished section do they see '1 review due'. Nobody outside the app is told; the review exists only if the student stumbles into it.
findings.fix: Surface due learn-mode reviews on HomeScreen and on the CompletionScreen itself ('Your review of this topic is due tomorrow at ...'). Once the schedule is server-side, add a daily email/push digest of due reviews. Also render the banner above the pre-test gate and completion screen, not just the step view.

findings.title: Explain It Back always reads 0/1 with an empty bar on every completion screen because the attempt callback is never wired
findings.evidence: onExplainAttempt is defined at line 45 but ExplainItBackUpgraded is rendered with only title, onAskTutor, isPremium (lines 390-391 and 428); the component signature is ({ title, onAskTutor, isPremium }) (ExplainItBackUpgraded.jsx:8). CompletionScreen.jsx:91 renders ScoreRow with score={{ correct: scores.explain.attempts, total: scores.explain.total || 1 }}, so it always shows 0/1, 0% width, labelled '20%'.
findings.studentImpact: Every student who answers at least one quiz or recall sees a 'Score Breakdown' in which 'Explain It Back 0/1' sits with an empty bar and a 20% weight, regardless of whether they wrote three paragraphs and got AI feedback. It reads as 'you failed this' or 'the app is broken'. Free users, who cannot get their explanation graded, are told they scored 0 on a component they were never allowed to complete.
findings.fix: Pass onExplainAttempt into ExplainItBackUpgraded and call it on submit (or on graded result for premium). Hide the Explain row when total is 0, and hide the 20% weight label unless a composite score is actually computed and shown.

findings.title: Strength meter maths guarantee a completed topic is amber on the completion screen, red within 2 days, ~11% after a week
findings.evidence: base = 20 + reviews*15 + quizAccuracy*20 + pretestScore*10 (line 42). On completion, recordReview(subjectId, sectionId, null) (LearnModeTab.jsx:214) sets reviews=1 and leaves quizAccuracy at 0 because InlineQuiz never calls recordReview (InlineQuiz.jsx has no strength import). Max base at completion is 35 (no/skipped pre-test) to 45 (3/3 pre-test). Green needs >=60 (line 55). Decay is base*0.85^days (line 48). Computed: base 35 -> 0d 35, 1d 30, 2d 25, 7d 11, 14d 4; base 45 -> 7d 14; even after a perfect spaced review (base 80) -> 7d 26, 14d 8. recordPretest sets lastReview = Date.now() (line 99), so the clock starts at the pre-test, before any learning. Sidebar.jsx:121 shows a small bar for every completed section.
findings.studentImpact: The first thing under 'Topic complete' is an amber bar saying '35% strength'. Coming back tomorrow it is 30%, then red. A student who completes five topics in a week sees a sidebar full of red slivers next to every green completion dot. The 14-day review interval the app schedules is incompatible with its own meter: by the time the review is due the meter says <10% even after a perfect previous review. Nothing the student does inside Learn Mode (inline quiz, explain-it-back, recalls, quick-fire, post-test) raises the meter except a SpacedReview or MixedReview.
findings.fix: Rebase the model: completion should land at a clearly positive value (e.g. 70-80) and decay should follow the scheduled interval (strength hits the 'review' threshold roughly when the review is due, not two days in). Feed inline quiz correctness, post-test and quick-fire results into quizAccuracy. Show 'Review due in N days' rather than a decaying percentage on the completion screen. Do not show a decaying bar in the sidebar next to a completion dot.

findings.title: Post-test and Quick Fire results are discarded: they never affect strength, the review schedule, or the server
findings.evidence: PostTest.handleSubmit (lines 34-38) only sets local state; no recordReview, no localStorage write, no fetch. QuickFireDrill has no persistence at all (no imports beyond react). The API accepts preTestScore/postTestScore (route.js line 16, 59-60) but saveLearnModeProgress never sends them (LearnModeTab.jsx:228-233).
findings.studentImpact: A student who does the post-test and goes 1/3 -> 3/3 sees 'Perfect score! You've mastered this topic', then the strength meter above it still says 35% and tomorrow's review is still due. Effort in the optional activities has no visible consequence anywhere else in the app.
findings.fix: On post-test and drill completion, call recordReview(subjectId, sectionId, score) and (once server-side) update the schedule: a strong post-test could push the first review from 1 day to 3.

findings.title: Score Breakdown is component state: it disappears on revisit and double-counts on Retry; weights 50/30/20 label a composite that is never computed
findings.evidence: scores lives in LearnModeTab useState (line 42), reset on remount. isComplete initialises from localStorage (lines 30-33) so a revisit renders CompletionScreen with scores all 0 and the breakdown hidden by the guard at CompletionScreen.jsx:86. onRetry (LearnModeTab.jsx:266-271) clears the flag and step but not scores, so a second run appends to the same counters. ScoreRow weights are static strings (lines 89-91); nothing sums them. The 'weakest area' callout (line 94) fires whenever quiz.correct < quiz.total, and quiz.total is one question per block (quizMap, lines 106-109).
findings.studentImpact: First time: a breakdown with 'Quiz 0/1 50%' and a warning 'Quiz questions need attention' after a single wrong click. Tomorrow: the same screen with no breakdown at all. After Retry: 'Quiz 1/2' even though they answered the single question right the second time. The percentages imply a mastery score the app never calculates.
findings.fix: Persist per-attempt scores with the completion record; reset scores in onRetry; drop the weight labels or compute and display the composite; require at least 3 quiz answers before the 'needs attention' callout.

findings.title: Recall score counts only attempted widgets; dismissing with the x is invisible
findings.evidence: ReorderRecall.jsx:75 and FillInRecall.jsx:66 dismiss via setDismissed(true) without calling onComplete; onComplete fires only on check (ReorderRecall.jsx:68, FillInRecall.jsx:56). onRecallResult (LearnModeTab.jsx:44) therefore never sees skips. Each recall can also appear twice (immediate at bottom, spaced at top of next step, lines 355-361 and 398-404), so a student who does both attempts of the same recall gets it counted twice.
findings.studentImpact: Skip nine reorders, check one: 'Recall 1/1' with a full bar. Do the same fill-in twice: 2/2. The number is technically not false but it does not measure what the label implies.
findings.fix: Report skips to the parent (onComplete(null) or an onSkip prop) and show 'Recall 1 of 10 attempted, 1 correct'; de-duplicate by recall prompt so the spaced re-attempt updates rather than appends.

findings.title: Same MCQ bank is reused for pre-test, inline quiz, spaced review (identical 5 forever), quick fire, and the Quiz tab; pre-test reveals the answers first
findings.evidence: PreTest highlights the correct option after submit (line 90) and stores the exact questions (lines 52-58) which PostTest re-asks verbatim (PostTest.jsx:23). handleComplete freezes 5 shuffled quiz questions into the schedule entry (LearnModeTab.jsx:206); SpacedReview uses reviewEntry.questions (ReviewMode.jsx:72) at every interval, and advanceReview caps at index 3 (line 44) with intervals[3]=14 so the entry is never retired (line 50). QuickFireDrill uses all quizData (QuickFireDrill.jsx:14); inline quiz draws from quizIndices of the same bank (LearnModeTab.jsx:106-109).
findings.studentImpact: A section with 8 MCQs: the student sees three of them (with answers revealed) before learning, sees them again inline, again in the post-test, again in quick fire, again in the Quiz tab, and the same 5 every 1, 3, 7, 14, 14, 14... days. 'Improvement' on the post-test mostly measures having seen the green highlight 20 minutes earlier. Reviews become answer-recognition, not retrieval.
findings.fix: Do not reveal correct answers on the pre-test (score only, or reveal after completion). Partition the bank: reserve questions not used in pre-test/inline for reviews, and re-sample review questions from the section at each interval rather than freezing them at completion. Retire an entry after the 14-day pass or extend to 30/60 days.

findings.title: Skipping the pre-test stores nothing, so the gate re-appears on the next visit at step 0
findings.evidence: 'Skip pre-test' calls onDone (line 119) which only sets showPretest=false in component state (LearnModeTab.jsx:253). The initialiser (lines 34-38) shows the gate whenever revvy_pretest_* is absent, !isResuming, and quizData exists; isResuming is true only when the saved step > 0 (StudyApp.jsx:639). Skipping also means hasPretestData is false so the 'Test your improvement' button never appears (CompletionScreen.jsx:114) and the +10 pretest strength (strength.js:42) is forfeited.
findings.studentImpact: Student skips, reads step 1, closes the tab. Comes back: pre-test again. Given 167 of 192 starters of 'introductory-concepts' never left step 0, a meaningful share of them may be hitting this gate repeatedly. A student who skips loses the post-test with no warning.
findings.fix: Record the skip (e.g. { skipped: true, timestamp }) so the gate is shown once; consider making the pre-test opt-in ('Want to test what you know first?') rather than a gate, and offer the post-test from a fresh sample when no pre-test exists.

findings.title: Quick Fire shows 'Time's up!' when the student picks option A
findings.evidence:
{answered && !selected && (
Time's up! The correct answer was highlighted.
)}. selected is the option index; choosing A sets selected=0, and !0 is true.
findings.studentImpact: Every time the student answers A (in time), the timeout message appears under the options, contradicting the feedback colours.
findings.fix: Use the last results entry: results[results.length-1]?.timedOut, or selected === null.

findings.title: Mixed review never advances the schedule and Review now only serves one entry per click
findings.evidence: MixedReview.handleSubmit calls recordReview per section (lines 217-219) but never advanceReview/saveSchedule, so due entries stay due. handleStartReview in StudyApp.jsx:334-339 opens due[0] only; after onFinish the count refreshes and the student must click again for the next.
findings.studentImpact: A student who does a 10-question mixed review still sees 'N reviews due' afterwards. With three overdue topics they must click 'Review now' three times.
findings.fix: Advance each section's schedule entry from the mixed review's per-section score; queue all due entries in one session.

strengths: Pre-test is skippable and the 0/3 copy is well judged: 'Perfect - your brain is now primed to learn this' (PreTest.jsx:131-135) frames failure as expected, and the submit button is disabled until every question is answered.
Pre-test questions are stored verbatim with the student's answers (PreTest.jsx:52-58), so the post-test compares like with like and PostTest degrades gracefully (returns null) when no data exists.
advanceReview (ReviewMode.jsx:39-58) is a sensible adaptive rule: >=60% moves out, <40% moves back, middle band holds; the intervals are stored on the entry so they can be tuned per section later.
handleComplete de-duplicates schedule entries (LearnModeTab.jsx:201) and 'Retry this topic' correctly clears the completion flag and returns to step 0 (LearnModeTab.jsx:266-271).
QuickFireDrill is polished: 200ms-tick timer, 5s urgency state, streak counter, auto-advance with a 300ms breather, and a summary with avg time and time-outs.
The completion screen gives a rich, coherent menu of next actions (post-test, drill, quiz, practice, flashcards, mixed review, retry, explore) and lists what was covered by block title.
The strength model deliberately includes a pre-test term and a decaying base, which is the right shape for a retrieval-strength meter; only the constants and inputs are wrong.
walkthrough: The student is on the last step and clicks 'Complete topic'. Synchronously: localStorage gets revvy_complete_<subject>_<section>=true; a review entry is pushed to revvy_review_schedule with 5 random MCQs from the section's quiz bank and nextDue = now + 1 day; recordReview sets reviews=1 and lastReview=now; a POST to /api/learn-mode/progress fires and fails inside Supabase (string into a boolean column) with no error surfaced. The step view is replaced by the Completion screen: green tick, 'Topic complete', the section title, then an amber strength bar reading '35% strength' (up to 45% if they aced the pre-test). If they answered at least one inline quiz or checked at least one recall, a 'Score Breakdown' appears: 'Quiz 1/2 50%', 'Recall 3/3 30%', and 'Explain It Back 0/1 20%' with an empty bar, always, because the callback is not wired. One wrong quiz click adds the warning 'Quiz questions need attention'. Below: 'What you covered' (block titles); 'Test your improvement' (only if they did not skip the pre-test; re-asks the same 3 questions, shows pre vs post, result is discarded); 'Quick fire drill (N questions)' (timed, all MCQs, result discarded; picking A shows a spurious 'Time's up'); 'Try the quiz' (preview-then-paywall for free users); links to /practice and /flashcards-practice; 'Mixed review' once 3 topics are completed; 'Retry this topic'; 'Explore this topic'; 'or choose another topic'. Tomorrow, on the same browser: opening this section lands straight on the Completion screen again, strength now 30%, no breakdown, and no mention that a review is due. Opening a different section shows the pre-test gate first; after submitting or skipping, the step view finally shows '1 review due - Review now', which runs a 5-question MCQ review, then 'Back to learning'. On a different device or after storage is cleared, none of this exists: no completion dot, no strength, no review, and the pre-test is suppressed only because the DB says they reached a step > 0.

findings.title: ExplainItBack is a silent dead end for free students; the tutor fallback button is unreachable for everyone
findings.evidence: Line 76 renders the grade button only when isPremium. Line 87 renders the tutor fallback only when (onAskTutor && !isPremium). StudyApp.jsx:696 passes onAskTutor={isPremium ? goToTutor : null}, so for free users onAskTutor is null and for premium users !isPremium is false: the 'Check my explanation with AI Tutor' button can never render. A free student sees toggle, one prompt sentence, a textarea, and nothing after typing: no submit, no save, no compare, no self-check, no paywall tease. Text is lost on step change (component keyed by currentStep, no persistence). Also LearnModeTab.jsx:45 defines onExplainAttempt but never passes it to the component (lines 390-391 and 428), so CompletionScreen.jsx:91 always shows Explain It Back as 0 out of 1 at 20% weight.
findings.studentImpact: On the last step of every block (including step 0 of introductory-concepts where 167 of 192 users are stuck) the student is invited to explain in their own words and gets zero response of any kind. At completion their Explain It Back score reads 0 regardless of effort.
findings.fix: For free users add a non-AI close-the-loop: after typing, reveal the block's section keyIdea values (already in content) as 'Compare with the key ideas' plus a 2-3 item self-check, and call onExplainAttempt. Wire onExplainAttempt into the component. Either delete the dead tutor branch or make it a real upsell that preserves the typed text. Persist the draft per block in localStorage.

findings.title: practiceIndices are resolved against a marks-sorted array, so 39 of 64 blocks show the wrong practice question
findings.evidence: Line 80: sortedPractice = practiceData sorted by marks ascending. Line 113: pMap[idx] = sortedPractice[pi] where pi comes from block.practiceIndices. Content authors index into raw practice[]. Checked all 43 sections in the dump: 64 blocks declare practiceIndices; 39 resolve to a different question under sorting. Example: economics__introductory-concepts block 'Production Possibility Frontiers' has practiceIndices [1]; raw practice[1] is the basic-economic-problem 6-marker, sortedPractice[1] is 'Outline two assumptions commonly made when constructing economic models' (raw index 4). The actual PPF 10-marker (raw index 2) lands under 'Economic Systems'. business__managing-people 'Motivation in Theory' gets 'Define span of control' instead of the Herzberg question.
findings.studentImpact: The practice question at the end of a block frequently has nothing to do with the block just studied, which makes the worked/guided/independent progression look random and undermines trust in the content.
findings.fix: Index practiceIndices into the raw practiceData array (or sort only for the legacy distributeItems fallback). Add a content-lint check that each block's referenced practice question shares vocabulary with the block title.

findings.title: maxTokens is not a valid option in AI SDK v6; every AI route runs with no output cap
findings.evidence: package.json pins ai ^6.0.116 (installed 6.0.116). node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts contains maxOutputTokens and zero occurrences of maxTokens. grade-explanation/route.js:57 passes maxTokens: 300, chat/route.js:120 passes maxTokens: 800, written-practice/evaluate/route.js:148 passes maxTokens: 800. In plain JS the unknown key is silently dropped.
findings.studentImpact: Grading output is uncapped (usually harmless since the schema is short, but a chatty model can run long and slow the 15s maxDuration). Tutor replies are capped only by the 'under 150 words' instruction; a model-answer request can stream a very long response and cost more than intended.
findings.fix: Rename to maxOutputTokens in all three routes. For grading use generateText with Output.object (zod schema) instead of regex parsing.

findings.title: Grading prompt is generic Edexcel A-Level, has no section content, no key ideas, no mark scheme, and no retry on parse failure
findings.evidence: System prompt line 48: 'You are a friendly Edexcel A-Level Economics & Business examiner' (not IAL). Prompt line 56 passes only topic (a block title such as 'The Nature of Economics') and the student text; no section keyIdea, body, misconception, or examMatters is sent, so the model grades against its own priors. Model is gemini-2.0-flash-lite (line 47) while chat and written-practice use gemini-2.5-flash-lite. Parsing at lines 61-66: greedy regex /\{[\s\S]*\}/ then JSON.parse; no structured output, no retry, any preamble with braces or a truncated response returns 500 'Could not parse AI response.'. No max length on explanation (only min 10 chars at line 41). No grounding means the 'gaps' list cannot reference what the notes actually said.
findings.studentImpact: A premium student's feedback can praise or penalise things the notes never covered, and cannot flag a misconception the section explicitly warns about. Parse failures surface as a generic error; the student must click Grade again manually (the button remains because feedback stays null).
findings.fix: Pass the block's section keyIdea, misconception and examMatters fields as grading context; say IAL; use Output.object with a zod schema and one automatic retry; cap explanation at ~1500 chars; align model with the rest of the app.

findings.title: InlinePractice never lets the student write; all three modes are read-only views of the same guidance text
findings.evidence: There is no textarea or input anywhere in the component. 'worked' (line 48) shows question.guidance paragraphs by default; 'guided' (line 63) shows the first guidance paragraph with a 'See full guidance' expander; 'independent' (line 85) hides the same guidance behind 'Reveal mark scheme'. The label copy 'We will walk you through this one' is the same mark-allocated skeleton, not an actual answer. The 'Get Full Model Answer from Tutor' button (lines 55, 78, 96) requires onAskTutor, which StudyApp:696 sets to null for free users, so free students never see a model answer or an upsell. Content itself is good: all 215 practice items have guidance with per-point mark annotations, e.g. the 20-mark PED question in economics__consumer-behaviour-demand.
findings.studentImpact: For a 20-mark Evaluate question a free student reads the question, clicks reveal, reads a mark-allocated skeleton, and moves on. No writing, no self-marking, no model answer. The 'practice' card practises nothing.
findings.fix: Add an optional answer box with a self-mark checklist generated from the guidance paragraphs (each '(n marks)' fragment becomes a tick box). Count it toward completion. For free users show the tutor button as a real paywall upsell rather than hiding it. The existing WrittenQuestionCard plus /api/written-practice/evaluate (already IAL AO-based) could be reused for premium.

findings.title: InlineQuiz: wrong answers feed only a local completion counter; confidence data is written but never read; remediation code is dead
findings.evidence: Line 30 calls onResult(correct); LearnModeTab.jsx:43 only increments scores.quiz for the CompletionScreen. Nothing is posted to the server, the mistakes tab, or the spaced review scheduler. Lines 55-66 write revvy_confidence_* to localStorage; grep across components, app and lib finds no reader. Lines 35-37 and 117-150 implement a remediation follow-up question, but 0 of 769 quiz items in the dump have a remediation field. The explanation is shown after 200ms (line 32-34), which is good. The confidence prompt auto-dismisses at 4s (lines 19-24), roughly the time it takes to read the median 205-char explanation, so students who read the explanation first lose the prompt.
findings.studentImpact: A student who gets the MCQ wrong sees the explanation, then the wrong answer vanishes from the system: it does not reappear in reviews, mistakes, or the post-test, and the 'How sure were you' click changes nothing later.
findings.fix: Feed wrong answers into the localStorage review schedule already created on completion, and into the mistakes tab for premium. Either author remediation questions or remove the dead code. Remove the 4s auto-dismiss or start it after the explanation is scrolled into view. Use confidence x correctness to prioritise the QuickFireDrill.

findings.title: Tutor system prompt has the wrong Economics unit range, no section content, and contradicts the practice guidance on essay structure
findings.evidence: Line 96: 'unit codes WEC11-WEC12' for Economics; IAL Economics is WEC11-WEC14. Lines 98-99 pass only section number/title and unit; no notes, keyIdea, or glossary is included, yet line 114 says 'Focus on the content in this section'. Line 112: 'For 20-mark essays: introduction not needed' while the practice guidance for 20-markers in the DB starts with 'Introduction: Define ... (2 marks)'. Streaming is correct (streamText + toUIMessageStreamResponse, gemini-2.5-flash-lite). TutorTab.jsx:236-239 empty state says 'AI Economics Tutor' and 'Edexcel IAS exam technique' for Business sections too; quickPromptsBySection (lines 5-80) has only Economics keys so every Business section gets the four generic prompts. On 429/403 the route returns a JSON body and the AI SDK DefaultChatTransport sets error.message to the raw response text (node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs:12622), so TutorTab.jsx:263 renders the literal JSON string.
findings.studentImpact: A premium Business student opens a tab titled AI Economics Tutor with Economics-flavoured framing. The tutor cannot reference what the student just read and can confidently give advice that differs from the notes and practice guidance. Hitting the daily limit shows a raw JSON blob.
findings.fix: Fix unit range to WEC11-WEC14; inject the section's keyIdeas and examMatters into the system prompt; align 20-mark structure guidance with content; make the empty-state copy subject-aware and add Business quick prompts; parse the JSON error body client-side or return plain text.

findings.title: In-memory rate limiter does not enforce limits on Vercel; chat route duplicates it with a second Map
findings.evidence: Line 7: const limiters = new Map() at module scope. On Vercel serverless each function instance holds its own Map; instances scale horizontally and are recycled after idle, so a user's count is scattered across instances and resets whenever a cold start happens. The file's own comment (lines 3-4) acknowledges this. chat/route.js:9-27 implements a separate in-memory checkRateLimit instead of importing this helper. Neither false-positive blocks a student in practice.
findings.studentImpact: No direct student harm; the 50/day grading and 30/day tutor limits are advisory only, so cost exposure is unbounded for a determined user. Not a cause of the step-0 drop-off.
findings.fix: Move both limits to a shared store (Supabase table with a daily counter, or Vercel KV/Upstash). Have chat/route.js import lib/rate-limit.js so there is one implementation.

findings.title: Subscription lookup uses .single(); a user with more than one user_subscriptions row is treated as free
findings.evidence: .single() at line 24 (and chat/route.js:47) returns an error and data null when more than one row matches; sub becomes undefined so isPremium is false and the route returns 403 'AI grading requires a Pro subscription.'. Whether duplicate rows exist in the live table was not verifiable from the read-only dump.
findings.studentImpact: If duplicates exist (e.g. a cancelled row plus an active row), a paying student sees the grade button (client AuthProvider may resolve differently) and then a 403 error on click.
findings.fix: Use .order('created_at', {ascending: false}).limit(1).maybeSingle(), or filter status = 'active' first. Verify with a count of user_id duplicates.

strengths: Practice guidance content is genuinely strong: all 215 practice items have mark-annotated, paragraph-structured guidance (e.g. the 20-mark PED question breaks out Introduction, elastic case, inelastic case, limitations, evaluation with marks per point). The problem is delivery, not content.
All 769 quiz items have a non-empty explanation (min 40 chars, median 205) and InlineQuiz reveals it 200ms after answering, with a two-phase reveal that is clear and fast.
The tutor route already frames itself as IAL, detects Business vs Economics from the unit code, uses KAAE mark-scheme language and command-word mark ranges, and streams correctly via the AI SDK.
Server-side premium checks exist on both AI endpoints, so the paywall cannot be bypassed from the client.
The grading response schema (grade, one-sentence feedback, strengths, gaps) is a good shape for a student-facing card, and the client renders it cleanly with colour-coded states.
A separate /api/written-practice/evaluate route already has a proper IAL AO1-AO4 rubric with per-mark-band expectations; it is a ready-made replacement for the weaker grade-explanation prompt.
walkthrough: A free student opens economics/introductory-concepts. Block 0 'The Nature of Economics' has two sections, so it is a single step (step 0) and isLastInBlock is true immediately. After the pre-test gate they see two NoteSections, then the Quick quiz ('Which of the following is a normative statement?'). They pick an option; 200ms later the correct answer highlights and the explanation appears; a 'How sure were you?' row shows and vanishes after 4 seconds. Their result increments a local counter and goes nowhere else. There is no practice card on this block (practiceIndices absent). Next they hit 'Explain it back: The Nature of Economics', a collapsed toggle. Expanding it shows one sentence of encouragement and a 4-row textarea with placeholder 'In my own words, this topic is about...'. They type. Nothing happens: no button appears (grade requires isPremium, tutor button requires onAskTutor which StudyApp sets to null for free users), no save, no comparison, no hint that upgrading would help. The Takeaway card below is the only thing they can compare against, but nothing prompts them to. If they click Next, the textarea unmounts and their text is gone. On block 2 ('Production Possibility Frontiers') they would meet a 'Worked example' practice card that shows the wrong question ('Outline two assumptions of economic models', because practiceIndices index into a marks-sorted array) with its mark-scheme skeleton pre-expanded and no place to write. At completion, the score breakdown shows Explain It Back 0/1 because the attempt callback is never wired.

findings.title: Progress rows are auto-written at step 0 on any section visit, and the saved value is the current step, not the furthest
findings.evidence: useEffect at 572-579 fires whenever `user && activeSection && sectionData?.content?.length` is truthy, independent of activeTab, and calls saveProgress(activeSection, learnModeSection, sectionData.content.length). The initial tab is 'overview' (line 262), so merely opening a section's launchpad upserts a user_content_progress row with furthest_step=0. The value passed is learnModeSection (the CURRENT step), so pressing Back overwrites 'furthest_step' with a smaller number. The only place the DB is consulted to restore position is handleSectionChange (634-638), which reads furthest_step.
findings.studentImpact: A student who clicks through the sidebar to look at three topics' overviews is recorded as having 'started' three topics at step 0. The live stat '825 of 1093 section starts never advanced past step 0' is therefore heavily inflated by overview visits and cannot be read as Learn Mode abandonment. A student who goes back two steps to re-read and then leaves resumes from the earlier step next time, not their furthest.
findings.fix: Only save when activeTab === 'learn-mode' and the student has actually rendered a step; send Math.max(prevFurthest, currentStep) (keep furthest separately in state), and have the API do GREATEST(furthest_step, new) on conflict.

findings.title: total_steps is the block count while furthest_step is a flat step index, so overview % and 'Completed' ticks are wrong on half the sections
findings.evidence: saveProgress(activeSection, learnModeSection, sectionData.content.length) sends the number of BLOCKS. LearnModeTab computes totalSteps = flatSteps.length (LearnModeTab.jsx:76), where each block yields ceil(sections.length/2) steps. In the live dump 21 of 43 sections have flat > blocks (e.g. economics macroeconomic-objectives-policies: 5 blocks / 11 steps; business financial-planning: 5 / 8; entrepreneurs-leaders: 4 / 7). SectionOverview computes progressPct = (furthest_step+1)/total_steps (StudyApp.jsx:53-55) and 'completed' = furthest_step >= total_steps-1 (431, 551); Sidebar renders the tick from savedProgress[id].completed (Sidebar.jsx:64, 127).
findings.studentImpact: On macroeconomic-objectives-policies a student at step 4 of 11 sees a green 'Completed' tick in the sidebar and 100% on the overview hero; at step 7 the hero text reads '160%' (the bar is clipped by overflow:hidden but the number is not). Progress the student can see contradicts the 'Step 7 of 11' counter inside Learn Mode.
findings.fix: Have LearnModeTab report its flatSteps.length up to StudyApp (e.g. via onStepChange({step,total})) and save that as total_steps; clamp progressPct to 100; backfill existing rows by recomputing total_steps from content.

findings.title: /api/learn-mode/progress can never write (string into boolean last_result) and even a successful write would be invisible to the dashboard
findings.evidence: Line 37 sets last_result: 'correct' and lines 57-58 set last_result: 'complete' / `post:${score}` and last_confidence: `pre:${score}` into practice_question_progress, whose last_result column is boolean. Neither upsert checks its error; the route returns { ok: true } regardless (line 65). LearnModeTab calls it fire-and-forget on every Next (LearnModeTab.jsx:158) and on completion (219). Separately, dashboard/route.js line 65 only strips the 'fc-' prefix (`row.section_id.replace(/^fc-/, '')`), so 'lm-<id>' rows would never map to a section for mastery, while the streak/overdue/recentActivity loops (lines 150-200) iterate all rows. The GET summary endpoint (lines 72-109) has no caller in the codebase.
findings.studentImpact: Nothing a student does inside Learn Mode reaches the server-side progress model. Zero rows with 'lm-' prefix exist in the live DB. The comment 'feeds into the learning progress dashboard' is false; if the column were fixed without also fixing the prefix handling, Learn Mode would start inflating streaks and 'Overdue' counts without touching mastery.
findings.fix: Either drop this endpoint and write Learn Mode events to user_content_progress (add completed_at, pretest/posttest columns), or create a dedicated learn_mode_progress table; check and log upsert errors; if keeping the lm- convention, strip it in the dashboard and decide explicitly whether Learn Mode steps count toward mastery and streak.

findings.title: Home 'Mastery', 'Streak', 'This Week' and /progress ignore Learn Mode, Quiz tab and Flashcards tab entirely
findings.evidence: total per section = quiz count + flashcard count (lines 48-52); mastered/learning come only from practice_question_progress (55-74). Writers of that table are /api/practice/progress (Smart Practice page) and /api/flashcards-practice/progress (Smart Flashcards page). The Quiz tab writes user_quiz_attempts (app/api/progress/quiz/route.js:14,37) and the Flashcards tab writes user_flashcard_progress (app/api/progress/flashcards/route.js:14,46); neither is read by the dashboard. Learn Mode writes nothing usable (see previous finding). HomeScreen renders masteryPct/streak/thisWeek from this payload (HomeScreen.jsx:123-126) and the local fallback hardcodes streak: 0 (line 59). ProgressDashboard labels every topic 'NEW' when total>0 and mastered=learning=0 (statusBadge lines 63-69) and shows 'No weak areas yet. Start practising!' (line 166).
findings.studentImpact: A student who completes every Learn Mode topic in Unit 1, scores well on inline quizzes and the completion Quick-Fire drill, opens Home and sees Mastery 0%, Streak 0, This Week 0, and every topic red at 0% labelled NEW. The product's own scoreboard tells the most engaged Learn Mode user they have done nothing. Because Learn Mode is the recommended 'START HERE' path, this is the default experience for most logged-in users.
findings.fix: Define one mastery model that ingests Learn Mode inline quiz/recall results, Quiz tab attempts and Flashcards tab reviews alongside Smart Practice; compute streak from any learning activity (including user_content_progress.updated_at); until then, hide the Mastery/Streak tiles for users with no practice rows rather than showing zeros.

findings.title: No exam date, unit selection, subject choice, or any onboarding after sign-up; new users land on the first Economics section's launchpad
findings.evidence: Callback redirects to searchParams.redirect || '/' (line 7); login does router.push(redirect) with default '/' (login/page.js:11). '/' mounts StudyApp with activeTab='overview' (StudyApp.jsx:262), subject = localStorage last-visited or subjects[0] (234-236), section = URL param, localStorage last-visited, or first section (255-259). Sidebar expands only Unit 1 (Sidebar.jsx:24-31). SettingsPage has only password and billing state (SettingsPage.jsx:7-13). grep across app/components/lib for examDate/exam_date/onboard/dailyGoal/reminder finds nothing outside globals.css. The Home tab (HomeScreen) is not the default and is only reachable via the sidebar logo button (Sidebar.jsx:70 onHomeClick).
findings.studentImpact: A Business student in an international school signs up, confirms email, and is dropped on 'Introductory Concepts' in Economics with 'RECOMMENDED · START HERE'. A Year 12 student taking only WEC11/WEC12 sees all four units and no way to say so. Nobody is asked when their exam is (Jan vs June series), so no countdown, pacing, or 'you have N topics and M weeks' framing exists. The 'introductory-concepts' section receiving 192 of 1093 starts is consistent with everyone being funnelled to the same first section regardless of subject or unit.
findings.fix: Add a 2-step first-run: pick subject (Economics/Business) and units being sat this series, plus exam session (Jan/June) and optional date; store in a user_profile table; make Home the post-login landing with a 'Next up' card computed from those choices.

findings.title: Every section change forces the Learn tab, which combines with the PreTest gate to interrupt browsing; HomeScreen/subject-switch navigation bypasses the resume logic and carries a stale step into the new section
findings.evidence: handleSectionChange sets activeTab 'learn-mode' (617) and is the ONLY path that resets learnModeSection from DB/localStorage (632-640). handleSubjectChange (596-613) sets 'learn-mode' but never resets learnModeSection or the URL. HomeScreen's onNavigateToSection prop is `(id) => { setActiveSection(id); setActiveTab('overview'); }` (664) and HomeScreen then calls onNavigateToTab('learn-mode') (HomeScreen.jsx:92,100,107,178), also never touching learnModeSection. LearnModeTab is keyed by section (676) but receives currentStep={learnModeSection} (686); step = flatSteps[currentStep] (LearnModeTab.jsx:296) is undefined when the stale index exceeds the new section's length, so neither render branch (343, 421) runs. The debounced save (572-579) then writes the stale step to the new section's DB row. PreTest shows whenever the localStorage key is absent and isResuming is false (LearnModeTab.jsx:35-39) and isResuming is only set in handleSectionChange.
findings.studentImpact: (a) A student reading Diagrams across five topics is bounced to Learn on each sidebar click and, for any topic they have not started, is met by a 3-question pre-test before seeing anything. (b) From Home, 'Continue Learning' or 'Practice <weak topic>' can open a section showing 'Step 9 of 5', a 180% progress bar, an empty body and a 'Complete topic' button. (c) Switching subject in the sidebar drops the student into the first section of the other subject at whatever step they were on before.
findings.fix: Route all section navigation through handleSectionChange (pass it to HomeScreen and use it in handleSubjectChange); preserve the current tab on section change when it is a free content tab (notes/diagrams/practice), defaulting to Learn only from the overview hero; clamp currentStep to totalSteps-1 inside LearnModeTab as a guard.

findings.title: Cross-device resume and pre-test state are localStorage-only; the DB step is never applied on first load
findings.evidence: learnModeSection initial state reads only localStorage (299-303); learnModeResuming starts false (304). savedProgress is fetched in an effect (418-437) but nothing applies it to learnModeSection for the initially active section; only handleSectionChange (634-638) does. PreTest done-state (`revvy_pretest_*`), completion (`revvy_complete_*`), review schedule (`revvy_review_schedule`), strength (`revvy_strength_*`) and inline quiz results (InlineQuiz.jsx:57-68) are all localStorage keys with no server copy.
findings.studentImpact: A student who worked on their laptop at school and opens the app on their phone at home lands on step 1 of the same section, is shown the pre-test again, sees no completion ticks or due reviews, and the Home 'Continue Learning' button does nothing if last-visited-section is missing (HomeScreen.jsx:178 silently no-ops). Everything that makes the app feel like 'their' app is tied to one browser.
findings.fix: On mount, once savedProgress arrives, set learnModeSection to max(local, db) for the active section and show the resume banner; persist pretest/completion/review-schedule to the server for logged-in users (a user_learn_state JSON column keyed by section would suffice).

findings.title: Nothing surfaces due spaced reviews outside the Learn tab, and the app runs two unconnected review systems
findings.evidence: Due-review banner renders only inside LearnModeTab (277-284) from localStorage revvy_review_schedule (ReviewMode.jsx:20-33). StudyApp computes dueReviewCount (319-332) but does not pass it to Sidebar, SectionOverview or HomeScreen. HomeScreen's 'Overdue' tile and 'Review N overdue cards' recommendation come from practice_question_progress.next_review (dashboard/route.js:147-154) and the action sends the student to /flashcards-practice (HomeScreen.jsx:86-87), not to the Learn Mode SpacedReview. No email, push, or reminder code exists in the repo.
findings.studentImpact: The 1/3/7/14-day reviews scheduled at topic completion (LearnModeTab.jsx:204-217) are only discoverable if the student happens to open Learn Mode on a day one is due. Nothing pulls them back: no email 'your Demand review is due', no badge on the sidebar or Home. Median activity span of about one hour for practice users is consistent with a product that has no return trigger.
findings.fix: Show a due-review count on Home and in the sidebar header; consolidate the two schedules (move Learn Mode review entries to the server); add a daily digest email via Supabase edge function or Resend for users with due reviews or an approaching exam date.

findings.title: Inside Learn Mode the premium delta is nearly invisible: free users never see the locked buttons, and a dead branch means they get no feedback and no upsell after 'Explain it back'
findings.evidence: StudyApp passes onAskTutor={isPremium ? goToTutor : null} (StudyApp.jsx:696). InlinePractice renders its 'Get Full Model Answer from Tutor' buttons only when onAskTutor is truthy (InlinePractice.jsx:52,75,96), so free users see no button at all. ExplainItBackUpgraded shows 'Grade my explanation' only for isPremium (76-84); the fallback at 87 is `onAskTutor && !isPremium` which can never be true because onAskTutor is null whenever !isPremium. Everything else in Learn Mode (NoteSection, InlineDiagram, InlineQuiz, recalls, TakeawayCard, PreTest/PostTest, QuickFireDrill over the full quizData, SpacedReview) is ungated. CompletionScreen's 'Try the quiz' (line 127) routes free users to the Quiz tab preview (2 questions, QuizTab.jsx:15) and then a PaywallOverlay.
findings.studentImpact: A free student types a 200-word explanation and the box just sits there: no grade, no 'unlock AI feedback' prompt, no acknowledgement. They finish a topic, drill all 25 quiz questions for free in Quick Fire, click 'Try the quiz' and hit a paywall for the same 25 questions. The premium offer looks arbitrary from inside the core loop, and the one moment of highest motivation (completion) ends in a wall rather than a next topic.
findings.fix: Render disabled/locked versions of 'Grade my explanation' and 'Model answer from Tutor' for free users with a one-line value prop and a trial CTA; fix the dead branch; on CompletionScreen, make the primary CTA 'Next topic' and demote or gate-label 'Try the quiz'; decide whether Quick Fire over the full bank should remain free given the Quiz tab is paywalled.

findings.title: Overview says '{blocks} steps' while Learn Mode counts flat steps, so the numbers disagree on screen
findings.evidence: SectionOverview shows contentSteps = sectionData.content.length (44, 79, 107). LearnModeTab shows 'Step N of {flatSteps.length}' (LearnModeTab.jsx:76, 331). The Content card uses `{notesSections || contentSteps} sections` (112), mixing the notes array length with block count.
findings.studentImpact: On business financial-planning the launchpad promises '5 steps'; clicking Start shows 'Step 1 of 8'. The student's first data point about how long a topic takes is wrong by 60%.
findings.fix: Compute the flat step count once (shared util from learn-mode/utils) and use it in both places; or drop the count and show estimated minutes.

findings.title: Free vs premium messaging contradicts itself across overview, upgrade page and paywall
findings.evidence: Upgrade page lists 'Model answers for every topic' under premium 'ONLY ON REVVY' (108-110), while SectionOverview places Model Answers under free 'EXAM RESOURCES' (StudyApp.jsx:137-146) and ModelAnswersPage paywalls inline at line 367. PaywallOverlay says 'No credit card for trial' (163) and upgrade page 'No card needed' (168), but checkout only sets payment_method_collection 'if_required' and trial_period_days for first-time subscribers (checkout/route.js:178-181); the overview CTA bar and category header still say '3-DAY FREE TRIAL' (StudyApp.jsx:167, 203) to anyone !isPremium, including the 40 free/cancelled users who already used it. Upgrade page's trust row claims '1,200+ Edexcel IAL students' (164) while live data shows 211 users with progress and 62 subscription rows.
findings.studentImpact: A student told 'no card needed' who is then asked for a card (because they trialled last term) loses trust at the checkout. A student who read 'Model answers' as free on the overview hits a paywall on the page. The audience is 16-18-year-olds paying with parents' cards; inconsistent claims are the kind of thing that ends in a chargeback or a bad word in a school group chat.
findings.fix: Single source of truth for the feature matrix (one constant consumed by overview, upgrade page, paywall); pass trialEligible from /api/subscription and switch copy to 'Subscribe' when false; verify or remove the 1,200+ claim.

findings.title: 'content' tab exists in the app but not in the tab bar, leaving no active tab and no obvious way back
findings.evidence: FREE_TABS includes 'content' with the comment 'kept for sidebar access' (25), but allTabs (29-40) has no 'content' entry. It is reached from Sidebar 'Content Explorer' (Sidebar.jsx:168), the overview 'Content' card (StudyApp.jsx:109), Learn Mode's '☰ View all content' (LearnModeTab.jsx:336) and CompletionScreen 'Explore this topic' (151). AnimatedTabBar renders only tabs in allTabs, so none is highlighted.
findings.studentImpact: Student clicks 'View all content', the tab strip shows nothing selected, and 'Learn' looks un-selected even though they were just in it. Mild disorientation on a screen that is meant to reduce it.
findings.fix: Either add Content to the tab bar (free) or retire it and route 'View all content' to Notes.

findings.title: Two competing completion indicators in the sidebar that disagree, and anonymous users get only one
findings.evidence: Rows render a localStorage-driven learnModeCompletions dot plus StrengthMeter (119-124) AND a DB-driven status tick from savedProgress.completed (125-139), whose threshold is the buggy block-count comparison. getSectionStatus returns null when !user (51), while learnModeCompletions is populated from localStorage for everyone (StudyApp.jsx:307-316).
findings.studentImpact: A section can show a clock 'In progress' icon next to a green 'Learn Mode complete' dot, or a 'Completed' tick with no dot. Students learn to ignore both.
findings.fix: Show one status derived from a single source (server for logged-in, local otherwise) once total_steps is fixed.

findings.title: Recommendation card tells brand-new users to 'Continue where you left off'
findings.evidence: getRecommendation returns type 'start' only when data is null (line 6). For a logged-in user the dashboard fetch succeeds with overdueCount 0 and weakestTopics [] and falls through to 'continue' (14): 'Continue where you left off / Keep building your knowledge'.
findings.studentImpact: First ever visit to Home reads as if they have history they do not have; the one place that could say 'Start with Unit 1, Topic 1' instead says 'continue'.
findings.fix: Treat overall.total===0 or no user_content_progress rows as 'start' and point at the first section of the chosen subject/unit.

findings.title: isPremium is false until /api/subscription (which calls Stripe twice) resolves, so premium users briefly see padlocks and the Tutor paywall
findings.evidence: AuthProvider starts with subscription null so isPremium is false (AuthProvider.jsx:25, 101) and fetches on every mount (55-57). For any user with stripe_customer_id the route awaits two stripe.subscriptions.list calls (14-17, 60-75) before responding. StudyApp renders PaywallOverlay for PREMIUM_TABS when !isPremium (645-648) and AnimatedTabBar shows padlocks when tab.premium && !isPremium.
findings.studentImpact: A paying student who reloads on the Tutor tab sees the 'Unlock Tutor' paywall for the duration of two Stripe round-trips, then it disappears. It reads as 'my subscription broke'.
findings.fix: Seed isPremium server-side (layout already fetches the user; fetch the subscription row too and pass as initialSubscription), and move Stripe reconciliation to a webhook/cron rather than every GET.

strengths: handleSectionChange (StudyApp.jsx:615-641) is a solid resume path: prefers DB furthest_step over localStorage, sets a resume banner with Continue / Start over, and replaceState()s the URL so refresh keeps the section.

The Section Overview launchpad (StudyApp.jsx:43-213) is a clear first screen: 'RECOMMENDED · START HERE' hero, explicit FREE / EXAM / PREMIUM groupings, padlocks on locked cards, per-section counts, and a single price line.

The free tier is generous and the core Learn Mode loop (notes, inline diagram, inline MCQ, practice with mark scheme, recall, takeaway, completion screen, post-test, quick-fire drill, 1/3/7/14-day spaced review) is entirely free; the paywall does not block learning.

Subscription resilience: /api/subscription self-heals DB vs Stripe drift both ways, checkout blocks duplicate purchases and trial abuse, and AuthProvider polls for 60s post-checkout with an explicit failure banner (AuthProvider.jsx:60-99).
Progress saves are debounced and optimistic (setSavedProgress before fetch), and progress writes are user-scoped upserts with onConflict keys.
Sidebar auto-expands only the active unit and collapses others (Sidebar.jsx:33-43), keeping a 40+ section tree manageable on mobile.
Subject-aware tab filtering (Diagrams only for Economics, Mistakes only for Business) avoids showing empty tabs.
Keyboard arrow navigation with a one-time hint, and careful scroll-reset handling for iOS Safari (StudyApp.jsx:467-501).

Home tab, /progress and the sidebar Resources give returning students several entry points; the dashboard code itself (streak, 7-day activity, weakest topics) is well structured and would be valuable once it is fed by Learn Mode.
walkthrough:
Minute 0-1: A student in Kuala Lumpur taps 'Create Account' on /signup, enters email + password, sees 'Check Your Email', opens the link. /auth/callback redirects to '/'. No welcome, no 'which subject / which units / when is your exam'. StudyApp mounts with activeTab='overview' on subjects[0] (Economics) and its first section (Introductory Concepts) unless a stale last-visited-section is in this browser. A Business student now has to notice the Economics/Business toggle at the top of the sidebar. The header shows 'Section 1 · Unit 1' and a tab strip: Home, Learn, Notes, Diagrams, Practice, then padlocked Flashcards, Quiz, Tutor, Extras. The Home tab is not where they landed; it only appears if they click the logo.

Minute 1-2: The overview says 'RECOMMENDED · START HERE — Learn Mode — Free — 5 steps'. The moment this page rendered, a user_content_progress row was written for this section at step 0 (they have not clicked anything). They click Start learning. Because the section has a quiz bank and no pretest key in localStorage, the first thing they see is a 3-question pre-test about content they have not read, with a small 'Skip pre-test' link. Most answer or skip.

Minute 2-4: Step 1 of 5 appears (on this section flat steps equal blocks; on half the catalogue it would say 'Step 1 of 8' against the '5 steps' promise). They read two note sections, hit an immediate recall widget at the bottom, press Next. On the last step of a block they get a diagram, one MCQ, a practice question with mark scheme, and an 'Explain it back' box. If they type an explanation, nothing happens: no grade, no tutor button, no hint that premium would grade it. The Next button posts to /api/learn-mode/progress, which fails silently on a boolean column; the debounced save to user_content_progress records their current step against a block-count total.

Minute 4-5: Curious, they click a different topic in the sidebar to peek at its diagrams. The app forces them into Learn Mode for that topic and, since it is unstarted, another pre-test. They go back to Home via the logo: 'Good evening, student', a card saying 'Continue where you left off' (on their first visit), and four tiles reading Streak 0, Mastery 0%, This Week 0, Overdue 0, with every topic listed red at 0%. Nothing they just did moved any of these numbers, and nothing will until they use Smart Practice or Smart Flashcards. They close the tab. No email, notification, or due-review badge will bring them back; the 1-day spaced review scheduled for the topic they finished is visible only if they happen to reopen Learn Mode tomorrow on the same browser.

First-time student, economics/introductory-concepts (5 blocks x 2 sections = 5 flat steps; 25 quiz, 5 practice, 3 diagrams). They arrive on the Learn tab by default (StudyApp.jsx:625). Within ~1s a DB row furthest_step=0/total_steps=5 is written before they have read anything (StudyApp.jsx:571-579). Screen 1 is the PreTest: 3 MCQs drawn at random from the whole 25-question bank, so they may be asked about the price mechanism (taught on step 5). 'Check my answers' is disabled until all 3 are answered; 'Skip' works but writes nothing, so the gate can reappear later. Step 1 of 5 (progress bar already reads 20%): no chapter heading; h2 'Economics as a social science' (key idea, paragraphs, flow, real example, misconception, exam-matters) then h2 'Positive and normative statements' — ~608 words. Then a Quick quiz (quiz[0]), no practice (block 0 has no practiceIndices), an 'Explain it back' box titled 'The Nature of Economics' (a title never shown on the page), a 3-item Takeaway, and finally a Reorder recall for section 0 ('Observe human behaviour / Build a simplified model / Apply ceteris paribus / Isolate the variable of interest' — an order that is not really sequential). The fill-in recall for 'positive-and-normative' is NOT shown here. Click Next: node turns to a tick for 350ms, then the page jumps instantly to the top of step 2 with no enter animation. Step 2 of 5 (40%): the very first thing under 'Step 2 of 5', above any heading, is a Fill-in-the-blanks about positive/normative statements, labelled only 'Quick Recall — Fill in the Blanks' with no hint it belongs to the previous step. Then h2 'The basic economic problem', h2 'Opportunity cost' (~594 words), quiz[1], a Worked example practice (p0 'Define opportunity cost', 4 marks, guidance fully revealed because it is the first practice step), Explain it back 'Scarcity, Choice and Opportunity Cost', Takeaway, then a Reorder recall (Unlimited wants → Scarcity → Choices → Opportunity cost — this one is a genuine chain). Step 3 of 5 (60%): Fill-in about opportunity cost at the top, then 'The PPF model' + 'Shifts of the PPF' (~619 words), the PPF diagram card (static, 'Tap to enlarge'), quiz[2], then a 'Guided practice' card that is sortedPractice[1] = 'Outline two assumptions commonly made when constructing economic models' (4 marks) — unrelated to PPF because practiceIndices index a marks-sorted array; the real PPF 10-marker (practice[2]) never appears in Learn Mode. Explain it back 'Production Possibility Frontiers', 4-item Takeaway, Reorder recall for the-ppf-model. Each step is roughly 600 words plus 5-7 widgets, i.e. 8-12 minutes, while the stepper says 'Step 3 of 5'. If they press Back to step 1 after having skipped the pretest, the PreTest gate reappears.
strengths: Pinned path (LearnModeTab.jsx:93-114) validates quizIndices/practiceIndices ranges and uses used-sets, so a quiz/practice item never appears twice in one section.

matchDiagramsToBlocks (learn-mode/utils.js:31-57) is strict: it never places an unrelated diagram on a block, and the 21 unpinned (legacy-path) sections all happen to use 2-section blocks so block index == flat-step index and the legacy mapping is coherent there (verified by simulation: 0 diagrams on wrong steps, 0 quiz/practice dropped).
Every recall widget is dismissable (ReorderRecall.jsx:20, FillInRecall.jsx:14) and PreTest is skippable (PreTest.jsx:127), so no widget hard-blocks progress.
navigateToStep guards double-clicks with isTransitioning (LearnModeTab.jsx:148) and scrollToTop targets both .tab-content and window (137-142), so the new step always starts at the top.
Worked → guided → independent practice fading (getPracticeMode, LearnModeTab.jsx:125-132; InlinePractice.jsx) is a sound scaffolding idea.
Progress works logged-out via localStorage (StudyApp.jsx:299-305, 397-404) and LearnModeTab is keyed by section (StudyApp.jsx:672) so per-section state resets cleanly.
InlineQuiz reveal sequence, confidence prompt with auto-dismiss, and remediation question (InlineQuiz.jsx) are well thought out and do not block navigation.

findings.title: Same recall shown twice back-to-back on every single-section step
findings.evidence: currentRecalls = step.sections.map(s => s.recall) (346); immediate recall renders currentRecalls[0] at the bottom (398-404). prevRecall = prevStepData.sections[prevStepData.sections.length - 1]?.recall (348-350) renders at the top of the next step (355-361). When a step has exactly one section, sections[0] === sections[last], so the identical recall object is rendered as `immed-N` then 350ms later as `spaced-N+1`. ReorderRecall uses recall.shuffled deterministically (ReorderRecall.jsx:10) so even the shuffle is identical. Across the live dump: 61 of 237 flat steps are single-section; 45 of those are non-final and carry a recall, i.e. 45 exact consecutive duplicates. Example: measures-economic-performance block 'Gross Domestic Product (GDP)' > gdp-per-capita reorder appears at the bottom of step 2 and again at the top of step 3. Both fire onRecallResult (44) so the CompletionScreen 'Recall' score double-counts.
findings.studentImpact: Student completes a reorder, clicks Next, and the first thing on the new step is the exact same reorder in the exact same shuffled order. Feels like a bug, trains them to dismiss recalls, and inflates the recall score on the completion screen.
findings.fix: Compute prevRecall only from a previous-step section that was NOT already used as that step's immediate recall (e.g. if prevStep.sections.length === 1, prevRecall = null), or switch to: immediate = every section's recall on its own step, spaced = a recall from >= 2 steps back.

findings.title: Second section's recall is deferred to the next step, and never shown on the final step
findings.evidence: Only currentRecalls[0] (sections[0].recall) is rendered on the current step (398). sections[1].recall is only reachable as prevRecall on step N+1 (348-350). On the last flat step there is no N+1, so sections[1].recall is never rendered. 10 of 43 sections end with a 2-section step; e.g. introductory-concepts block 'Economic Systems' > the-price-mechanism (fillin) is never shown anywhere. The 'spaced' recall is also only 350ms after the content (157-163), so it is not spaced.
findings.studentImpact: Half the authored recall exercises appear before the student has seen any heading on the new step, and the last block's second recall is silently lost. No true spacing happens.
findings.fix: Render every section's recall on the step that teaches it (after the section or at step end), and use the top-of-step slot for a genuinely older recall (2+ steps back or from the review schedule).

findings.title: Spaced recall is the first element on a new step, above the title, with no 'from last step' cue
findings.evidence: prevRecall widget is rendered at 355-361, before the <div className="lm-content"> that holds the h2 section titles (364-367). Both ReorderRecall and FillInRecall use the same header text 'Quick Recall — Reorder' / 'Quick Recall — Fill in the Blanks' (ReorderRecall.jsx:81, FillInRecall.jsx:67) regardless of slot; the recall.prompt is generic ('Put these in the right order:', 'Complete the chain:'). Nothing on screen names the section the recall belongs to.
findings.studentImpact: Student lands on 'Step 2 of 5' and is immediately asked to fill blanks about positive/normative statements with no heading telling them what step 2 is about. This is the single biggest source of the 'disjointed' feeling.
findings.fix: Either move the spaced recall below the new content, or wrap it in a card header like 'Recall from step 1: Positive and normative statements' using prevStepData.sections[last].title, and show the step's headings first.

findings.title: Block (chapter) title is never rendered on structured steps
findings.evidence: step.blockTitle is set at 61 but the only use is as the ExplainItBack title (389-391). The structured branch (344-405) renders h2 sec.title per section and no block heading. Legacy branch does render block.title (410).
findings.studentImpact: In measures-economic-performance step 2 the student sees only h2 'GDP per capita' and is then asked to 'Explain it back: Gross Domestic Product (GDP)' — a title they have never seen. No sense of which chapter they are in or how many steps it spans.
findings.fix:
Render a block eyebrow on every structured step (e.g. `
{step.blockTitle} · part {n} of {m}
` above the first h2) and use isFirstInBlock to style chapter starts.

findings.title: practiceIndices resolve against a marks-sorted array, so the pinned practice question is usually the wrong one
findings.evidence: sortedPractice = [...practiceData].sort((a,b) => a.marks - b.marks) (80); step.practiceIndices.find(i => ... i < sortedPractice.length ...) then pMap[idx] = sortedPractice[pi] (110-112). Authored indices refer to practice[] order. Across the dump, 39 of 64 practiceIndices resolve to a different question than practice[i]. introductory-concepts: practice marks in authored order are [4,6,10,20,4]; block 'Production Possibility Frontiers' practiceIndices [1] → sortedPractice[1] = practice[4] 'Outline two assumptions commonly made when constructing economic models' (4 marks); block 'Economic Systems' practiceIndices [2] → sortedPractice[2] = practice[1] 'Explain two reasons why the basic economic problem is relevant...'. The PPF 10-marker (practice[2]) and 20-marker (practice[3]) never appear in Learn Mode.
findings.studentImpact: The 'Guided practice' on the PPF step is about model assumptions; the 'Quick check' on Economic Systems is about the basic economic problem. Questions look randomly attached to the wrong topic.
findings.fix: Index practiceIndices into the original practiceData (`practiceData[pi]`) and drop the sort in the pinned path; keep the sort only for the legacy distributeItems fallback.

findings.title: diagramRef pinning matches only 15 of 39 refs and disables the title fallback, leaving 15 sections with zero diagrams in Learn Mode
findings.evidence: hasRefs = flatSteps.some(s => s.diagramRef || s.quizIndices || s.practiceIndices) (86); if true, diagrams are placed only by substring match of diagramRef vs diagram.title (97-105) and matchDiagramsToBlocks is never consulted (115-120). Blocks without a diagramRef get nothing. In the dump 39 blocks have a diagramRef, 15 match; only 15 of 81 diagrams in pinned sections reach Learn Mode. measures-economic-performance: block 'Inflation: Causes and Effects' has diagramRef 'Demand-Pull and Cost-Push Inflation' (no such diagram); the two real diagrams 'CPI Basket of Goods' and 'Types of Unemployment' are unreferenced, so the section shows no diagram at all. Same for aggregate-demand (3), economic-growth (3), macroeconomic-objectives-policies (4), market-structures-contestability (5), etc. Missing/out-of-range indices at 107/111 are dropped silently with no fallback.
findings.studentImpact: Diagram-heavy macro topics show no diagram during learning even though the Diagrams tab has them; a broken ref in one block silently hides the diagram.
findings.fix: Fall back per block: if diagramRef is absent or unmatched, try matchDiagramsToBlocks word-overlap for that block; add a build-time/admin check that every diagramRef resolves. Same per-block fallback for quizIndices (currently 55/170 blocks have none).

findings.title: DB progress stores current step (not furthest) against BLOCK count, so completion/percent are wrong for any section with 3+-section blocks
findings.evidence: saveProgress(activeSection, learnModeSection, sectionData.content.length) (575) — learnModeSection is the flat step index (LearnModeTab pairs sections 2-per-step, 48-75), content.length is the block count. completed = furthestStep >= totalSteps - 1 (551, 431). SectionOverview percent = (furthest_step + 1) / total_steps (54). Dump: 237 flat steps vs 170 blocks. measures-economic-performance: 16 steps / 8 blocks → 'completed' at step 8 (halfway), overview shows 113%..200%. Meanwhile LearnModeTab.jsx:156 posts flat totalSteps to the other endpoint, so two different 'total' definitions exist. 'furthest_step' is overwritten with the current step on Back, 'Start over' (LearnModeTab 304), 'Restart learning' (333) and CompletionScreen retry (269), so it is a position pointer, not a high-water mark. handleStepChange (StudyApp 581-594) which does track furthestStep is never called by LearnModeTab (onStepChange={setLearnModeSection}, 687).
findings.studentImpact: Overview card says 150% / 'completed' halfway through a topic; pressing Start over wipes progress; cross-device resume lands on wrong step; progress analytics are unreliable.
findings.fix: Have LearnModeTab report { activeStep, furthestStep: max(prev, step), totalSteps: flatSteps.length } via onStepChange/handleStepChange, persist furthest = Math.max(existing, step) server-side, and clamp percent to 100.

findings.title: A progress row at step 0 is written on every section open, before the student reads anything
findings.evidence: useEffect deps [learnModeSection, activeSection, user, sectionData, saveProgress] (579) runs on mount and again when sectionData loads, posting furthest_step: 0 after 1s. Every section change lands on 'learn-mode' (625) and the PreTest gate is shown while currentStep === 0 (LearnModeTab 249). So a row with furthest_step 0 exists for anyone who clicked a section in the sidebar, including users still on (or bouncing from) the pretest.
findings.studentImpact: Not a student-facing bug, but it means the '75% never advanced past step 0' metric conflates 'opened the section' with 'started learning and stalled', and cannot distinguish pretest abandonment from step-1 abandonment.
findings.fix: Only save when learnModeSection changes from a user action (skip the initial effect run, or save from navigateToStep), and record a separate event for pretest done/skipped.

findings.title: Skipping the PreTest is not persisted; the gate reappears on Back-to-step-1, Restart, Retry and reload
findings.evidence: 'Skip pre-test' calls onDone only (127); the localStorage key revvy_pretest_* is written only in handleSubmit (46-58). In LearnModeTab, showPretest is state initialised once (34-38) and set false in onDone (253) — but the gate is `showPretest && currentStep === 0` (249). showPretest is only set false in memory, so after a reload it is true again; on this session, since it was set false it will not reappear, but on any later visit (isResuming false on initial page load, StudyApp 305) a student who skipped and is back at step 0 (Back button 436, 'Restart learning' 333, CompletionScreen onRetry 269→onStepChange(0)) gets the PreTest again. Additionally, the keydown listener (174-182) is registered before the PreTest early return, so ArrowRight during the pretest silently navigates to step 2 and the pretest vanishes.
findings.studentImpact: A student who skipped the pretest and later presses Back or Restart is suddenly shown 'Quick pre-test' mid-topic; on desktop, an accidental arrow key during the pretest jumps them into the middle of the content.
findings.fix: Write the revvy_pretest key with {skipped:true} on skip; only show the gate when currentStep === 0 AND the section has never been started; ignore keyboard nav while showPretest or isComplete.

findings.title: Keyboard navigation uses a stale closure and stays active on the PreTest and Completion screens
findings.evidence: useEffect deps are [currentStep, totalSteps] (182) but handleKeyDown calls navigateToStep, which reads isTransitioning from the render closure (148). Between a keypress and the 350ms swap, the listener still sees isTransitioning=false, so a second ArrowRight re-enters navigateToStep, fires a second saveLearnModeProgress (156) and a second timeout. The listener is attached regardless of showPretest (249) or isComplete (259) because hooks run before the early returns; ArrowLeft on the CompletionScreen changes currentStep and persists it (StudyApp 575) while the completion screen stays visible. Only INPUT/TEXTAREA are excluded (176), so arrow keys pressed while a reorder item button is focused still change step.
findings.studentImpact: Desktop students can skip past the pretest or lose an in-progress quiz/recall by pressing an arrow key; step counter can desync from what is on screen.
findings.fix: Use a ref for isTransitioning, include showPretest/isComplete in the guard, and ignore keydown when document.activeElement is inside .lm-recall-card/.lm-quiz-card or a modal.

findings.title: Step transition: 350ms freeze then hard cut; enter/exit animations are defined but never applied
findings.evidence: Forward nav: setStepComplete/setNodePopped, wait 350ms, scrollToTop(true) instant, onStepChange (157-163). Backward nav: instant swap with no feedback (164-170). globals.css:3328-3329 define .lm-stepper-content.step-exit / .step-enter (lmStepExit/lmStepEnter keyframes at 3260-3268) but no JSX ever adds those classes. The stepper rail shows a single node and one line whose 'filled' class is just currentStep > 0 (323); .lm-stepper-node has cursor:pointer (globals.css:1912) but no onClick.
findings.studentImpact: Every Next is a brief freeze followed by an abrupt jump to a page whose top is a recall widget; Back gives no acknowledgement. The rail looks clickable but does nothing and conveys no position.
findings.fix: Apply step-exit/step-enter classes around onStepChange, or drop the 350ms delay and use the enter animation only; render a real multi-node rail (or block-level dots) with onClick for visited steps.

findings.title: 2-per-step pairing yields ~600-word steps that also carry all end-of-block widgets, with an uneven 600/300 rhythm on 3-section blocks
findings.evidence: Pairing is by count (54-57), not by length or block boundary. Word counts (body+keyIdea+realExample+misconception+examMatters, excl. recall): introductory-concepts steps = 608 / 594 / 619 / 581 / 660 words, and because every block has 2 sections every step is also last-in-block, so each step = ~600 words + quiz + practice + ExplainItBack + Takeaway + immediate recall (+ spaced recall on top): 6-7 interactive widgets after 600 words. measures-economic-performance alternates 584-668-word steps (no widgets, one recall) with 279-330-word steps that carry every widget (diagram, quiz, practice, explain, takeaway, 2 recalls incl. the duplicate). 59 of 170 blocks have 3 sections, 6 have 4, 1 has 5. Progress bar = (step+1)/totalSteps (282) so it reads 20% before any reading on a 5-step section.
findings.studentImpact: Each step is an 8-12 minute wall; 'Step 1 of 5' feels misleadingly short; on 3-section blocks the short step is the heavy one, so effort per step is unpredictable. Combined with the pretest this explains stalling at step 0/1.
findings.fix: Make one section = one step (or pair only when combined words < ~350), keep end-of-block widgets on a dedicated 'check-in' step, and base the progress bar on flat steps + widgets completed.

findings.title: Resume banner only appears after an in-app section change, not on reload/deep link; DB pointer beats local pointer
findings.evidence: learnModeResuming defaults to false (305) and is set only in handleSectionChange (639); on initial URL load learnModeSection comes from localStorage (299-303) with no banner. In handleSectionChange, step = dbStep ?? localStep (632-637) — DB value (a current-position pointer, see other finding) wins even when localStorage is newer (e.g. the 1s debounce did not flush before navigating away).
findings.studentImpact: A student reloading at step 4 is dropped straight into step 4 with no 'continue or restart' choice; a student switching sections quickly can be sent back a step on return.
findings.fix: Compute isResuming from step > 0 on mount too; take Math.max(dbStep, localStep) and treat DB furthest as a high-water mark.

findings.title: /api/learn-mode/progress writes never succeed and its GET has no consumer
findings.evidence: last_result: 'correct' (38) / 'complete' | `post:${score}` (58) and last_confidence `pre:${score}` (59) are strings written to practice_question_progress where last_result is boolean (established: 0 'lm-' rows in live DB). LearnModeTab calls it on every forward nav and on completion (156, 217) with .catch(() => {}) (234). grep shows no component calls GET /api/learn-mode/progress, so the summary endpoint is dead code.
findings.studentImpact: None directly; one wasted failing request per step and a misleading 'feeds the progress dashboard' comment. Completion is only stored in localStorage (197), so it does not survive a device change.
findings.fix: Delete the endpoint or move completion + pre/post scores into user_content_progress (add completed_at, pretest_score, posttest_score columns) and read them in the dashboard.

findings.title: FillInRecall can never be completed for 6 live sections (Check stays disabled; only exit is the unlabelled ×)
findings.evidence: Two independent causes. (1) Duplicate answers: `availableWords = shuffledWords.filter(w => !placed.includes(w))` (line 16) removes EVERY chip equal to a placed word, so once 'Hawthorne' is placed, the second 'Hawthorne' chip vanishes; `allFilled = placed.every(w => w !== null)` (line 59) is never true and `<button ... disabled={!allFilled}>Check answers</button>` (line 119) stays disabled. Affected: business__managing-people > Motivation in Theory > mayos-human-relations ['Hawthorne','Hawthorne','Human Relations']; business__the-market > PED > ped-and-revenue ['increase','increase','price']; economics__consumer-behaviour-demand > Rational Decision Making > utility-and-utility-maximisation ['utility','utility','diminishes']; economics__consumer-behaviour-demand > PED > interpreting-ped-values ['elastic','inelastic','inelastic']. (2) blankIdx is computed per template PART (line 72: `recall.template.slice(0,i+1).filter(p => p.includes('___')).length - 1`) but `placed` is sized to `recall.answers` (line 6). business__managing-people > Organisational Design > hierarchy-and-span-of-control has 3 parts but 5 answers ['Span','control','Chain','command','narrow']; matrix-structures has 3 parts, 4 answers. Only 3 slots can ever be filled, so allFilled is permanently false.
findings.studentImpact: Student fills the visible blanks, the Check button stays greyed out with no message, the word bank has disappeared, and the only way out is the × in the corner. Nothing tells them the widget is broken; it reads as 'I did something wrong'.
findings.fix: Track placement by chip index, not word string (`placed` holds indices into shuffledWords; availableWords filters by index). Validate at content load or in a script: number of '___' occurrences across template must equal answers.length and each part must contain at most one '___' (or make blankIdx count '___' occurrences, not parts). Add a content-lint that fails on the 6 sections above.

findings.title: Multi-word blanks written as '___ ___' silently delete the rest of the sentence (10 template lines across 8 sections)
findings.evidence: `const [before, after] = part.split('___');` keeps only the first two segments. For business__managing-people > Approaches to Staffing > employer-employee-relationships the part '___ ___ represent workers collectively in negotiations' splits to ['', ' ', ' represent workers…'] and the third segment is dropped.
