Same for: '___ ___ is the process of negotiating agreements…' (same section), selection-methods ('… combine exercises, group tasks…' lost), hierarchy-and-span-of-control x2 ('… is the number of subordinates…', '… is the path along which decisions flow…' lost), matrix-structures ('… manager' lost), mayos-human-relations ('… school emphasised teamwork…' lost), leadership-styles ('___-___ leaders take a hands-off approach…' → renders '[blank]-' only), opportunity-cost ('… forgone' lost), economics__introductory-concepts > Specialisation… > money-and-exchange (', and standard of deferred payment' lost).
findings.studentImpact: The fill-in line reads as a bare blank with no sentence, e.g. just '[____]' or '[____]-'. The student has no cue what the blank means and the 'store of value, unit of account, standard of deferred payment' chain loses its third function.
findings.fix: Render all segments: `part.split('___')` → interleave text segments with blanks, incrementing a running blank counter; or normalise content so a multi-word answer uses a single '___'. Add the lint from the previous finding.

findings.title: 62% of diagramRefs never match a diagram, so the block silently renders no diagram (24 of 39 refs; all 3 Business refs)
findings.evidence: Matching is title-substring only: `const t = (d.title||'').toLowerCase(); return t.includes(ref) || ref.includes(t);` (lines 101-103). Against the DB dump this matches 15 and fails 24, e.g. economics__aggregate-demand block 'The AD Curve' ref 'Aggregate Demand Curve' vs diagram titled 'The AD Curve'; 'Shifts in Aggregate Demand' (no such diagram); economics__economic-growth refs are slugs ('ad-as-growth','output-gap-diagram','trade-cycle-diagram') while diagram titles are prose ('Output Gap Diagram' fails because of the hyphen); economics__price-determination 'Indirect Tax'/'Subsidy'/'Consumer Surplus' vs 2 diagrams; macroeconomic-objectives-policies 'phillips-curve','fiscal-policy-ad' etc. Business: business__the-market blocks 'Demand…','Supply…','Market Equilibrium' carry refs 'demand-curve','supply-curve','equilibrium-diagram' but the section has 0 diagrams. Because `hasRefs` is section-wide (line 86) the legacy `matchDiagramsToBlocks` fallback is disabled once any block has a ref, so an unmatched ref yields nothing at `{step.isLastInBlock && currentDiagram && <InlineDiagram …/>}` (line 373). No placeholder or log.
findings.studentImpact: An Economics student finishing the 'Output Gaps' or 'The AD Curve' block, which the content author explicitly tagged for a diagram, sees no diagram at all; a Business student in The Market gets no demand/supply/equilibrium diagram even though the block asks for one. The founder's 'diagrams are passive' concern is preceded by 'diagrams are absent' for most tagged blocks.
findings.fix: Match on a stable diagram `id`/slug and normalise both sides (lowercase, strip non-alphanumerics) before substring comparison; in dev, `console.warn` unmatched refs; add a lint that reports refs without a diagram. Author the 3 missing Business diagrams or drop the refs.

findings.title: 'Spaced' recall is often the identical widget shown twice, seconds apart, and counted twice (54 of 237 steps)
findings.evidence: Immediate recall = `currentRecalls[0]` (first section of this step, lines 346, 398-403); spaced recall = `prevStepData.sections[last].recall` (lines 348-350, 355-360). Sections are paired 2-per-step (lines 52-56), so any step with a single section (odd-length blocks: 54 steps in the dump) has first === last, and the same recall is rendered at the bottom of step N and again at the top of step N+1 with `key={`immed-${currentStep}`}` / `key={`spaced-${currentStep}`}` so it is a fresh mount. Each mount calls `onRecallResult` (line 44) so it counts twice in scores.recall. ReorderRecall additionally starts from the same fixed arrangement every time (`recall.shuffled` is static JSON, ReorderRecall.jsx line 9), so the second showing is a memory of which taps to make. Back then Next also remounts and re-counts.
findings.studentImpact: Student answers a reorder, taps Next, and the first thing on the new screen is the same reorder in the same scrambled state. It feels like a bug, doubles the recall count on the completion screen, and the 'spaced' label is untrue (the gap is one tap).
findings.fix: Track answered recalls by section id in a Set; never render a recall that has been shown in the last N steps; for 1-section steps skip the immediate recall and rely on the spaced showing. Randomise the reorder start order on mount (seeded by attempt).

findings.title: Fill-in is a prefix-matching task, not recall: closed 3-word bank + 'Pr____' hints + answer words visible in the template
findings.evidence: Word bank is exactly `recall.answers` shuffled (line 12), 138 of 141 fill-ins have 3 answers for 3 blanks, so the last blank is forced by elimination and the first two are a 50/50. Hint (line 92, `recall.hints?.[blankIdx]`) is rendered inside the blank; 301 of ~420 hints are 2 letters + underscores and 89 are 3 letters (dump), e.g. 'Cr______','Ru_____','Ex_______' for Creating/Running/Expanding, and the underscore count leaks length. With the chips on screen, hint + chip is a visual match with zero retrieval. Numeric hints degrade to '10_'→'100', '2-_'→'2-3', '12___'→'12-18' (business__managing-finance > Understanding Profit > gross-profit; economics__macroeconomic-objectives-policies > … > economic-growth-objective, interest-rate-policy). In 36 sections an answer word is printed verbatim elsewhere in the template, e.g. business__financial-planning > Budgets > purpose-of-budgets: 'A budget sets ___ limits… Budgets help control spending and ___ … against the ___' with answers ['spending','motivate','budget'].
findings.studentImpact: A student who knows nothing about the topic scores 3/3 by matching first letters to chips. The score is inflated and the completion screen tells them recall is strong when it was never tested.
findings.fix: Add distractor chips (2-3 plausible wrong terms from the section's glossary) so elimination fails; make hints semantic ('the term for satisfaction from one more unit') or first-letter only without length; reject templates whose non-blank text contains an answer word; consider typed input with fuzzy match for premium.

findings.title: Dismiss (×) records nothing; the recall score on the completion screen only counts what the student chose to attempt
findings.evidence: `<button className="lm-recall-dismiss" onClick={() => setDismissed(true)} title="Skip">×</button>` (ReorderRecall.jsx line 75; FillInRecall.jsx line 66) sets state and the component `return null`s (line 20 / 14). `onComplete` is only called from `check()` (ReorderRecall.jsx line 68; FillInRecall.jsx line 56), so `onRecallResult` (LearnModeTab.jsx line 44) is never invoked: total is not incremented. `title="Skip"` is a hover tooltip, invisible on touch; no confirmation. CompletionScreen.jsx lines 86-92 then shows 'Recall 2/2 · 30%' if the student dismissed the other eight, and hides the whole breakdown if quiz.total and recall.total are both 0. The '30%' weight is a label only; nothing computes a weighted total.
findings.studentImpact: Dismissing is free and invisible, so the path of least resistance is to × every recall; the completion screen then either hides the score or reports a flattering ratio. Nothing is persisted (the /api/learn-mode/progress write fails per the product context), so dismissed recalls never come back as review items.
findings.fix: Treat dismiss as a skip: call `onComplete(null)` and track `{correct,total,skipped}`; show 'Skipped 6 recalls' on the completion screen and feed skipped ids into the 1/3/7/14-day review scheduler. Replace × with a visible 'Skip' text button.

findings.title: ReorderRecall gives one attempt, no retry, and 'Correct order' with no reason; a single wrong swap is a fail
findings.evidence: `check()` (lines 61-69) sets `checked=true`; `moveItem` (line 23) and `handleTap` (line 32) both early-return when `checked`, and the arrows are unmounted (`!checked && …`, line 103). Wrong state renders `✗ N of 4 in the right position` (line 141) and the plain list `Correct order: 1. … 2. …` (lines 115-124). The recall schema has no rationale field (dump: reorder = {prompt, correctOrder, shuffled} only), so nothing explains why B precedes C. A student with [A,C,B,D] (one swap off) gets '2 of 4', items 2 and 3 red, and cannot fix and re-check. `isRight` is positional (line 63) so an item that is off by one is marked as wrong as one that is reversed.
findings.studentImpact: Near-miss and total-miss look the same, and the only feedback is the answer key. The student learns 'I was wrong', not the causal chain the widget is supposed to teach, and cannot try again to consolidate.
findings.fix: Allow 'Try again' after a wrong check (keep correct items locked, unlock wrong ones); show partial-credit ('3 items are one place off'); add an optional `why` string per correctOrder item in content so the wrong-state panel can render a one-line rationale per step.

findings.title: 19 of 131 reorder prompts ask for an order that has no canonical answer
findings.evidence: Prompts matching rank/most/least/priority/typical/logical (dump scan): business__entrepreneurs-leaders > Entrepreneurial Motives… > non-financial-motives 'Rank these motives from most commonly cited to least'; > Business Objectives > common-objectives 'Put business objectives in typical order of priority as a firm develops'; business__financial-planning > Sales, Revenue and Costs > fixed-variable-costs 'Classify these costs from most fixed to most variable' (annual rent vs monthly insurance is arbitrary); > Sales Forecasting > factors-affecting-forecasts 'most to least predictable impact'; business__managing-finance > Causes of Business Failure > external-causes-of-failure 'most gradual to most sudden'; business__planning-raising-finance > Liability… > choosing-appropriate-finance 'Match the finance source to the most appropriate use' (a matching task forced into an ordering widget); economics__consumer-behaviour-demand > PED > factors-influencing-ped 'from most to least important'; > XED > interpreting-xed-values 'weakest to strongest' where the last item is a strong negative (magnitude vs sign confusion); economics__economic-growth > Output Gaps > negative-output-gap 'consequences in logical order' where items are simultaneous. 129 of 131 are exactly 4 items.
findings.studentImpact: A student who understands the topic can still be marked wrong for a defensible order, which is the demotivation the founder heard in feedback. It also teaches false precision (there is no spec-sanctioned ranking of PED factors).
findings.fix: Content rule: reorder only for genuine sequences (process steps, causal chains, calculation order). Convert rankings to a 'sort into two groups' or fill-in; convert 'match X to Y' to a pairing widget. Lint on prompt keywords rank/most/least/important/typical.

findings.title: Recall card text colours are hard-coded for dark theme; near-invisible in light theme
findings.evidence: `.lm-recall-prompt { color: #d4bfff }` (line 2704), `.lm-recall-hint { color: #d4bfff }` (2734), `.lm-word-chip { color: #d4bfff; background: rgba(167,139,250,0.12) }` (2780-2785), `.lm-recall-label { color: #a78bfa }` (2700-2703). The app ships a light theme (`:root, [data-theme="light"]` at globals.css line 14-15; ThemeProvider.jsx line 23 sets data-theme) and there are no light-theme overrides for any lm-recall/lm-word/lm-fillin selector (grep returned none). #d4bfff on a white card is roughly 1.5:1 contrast.
findings.studentImpact: A student who switches to light mode (common in bright classrooms, on phones in daylight) sees the recall prompt and the word-bank chips as faint lavender on white; the fill-in becomes unreadable.
findings.fix: Replace literal colours with tokens (`var(--accent-purple)`, `var(--text-secondary)`) and define light/dark values in the :root / [data-theme="dark"] blocks.

findings.title: Reorder arrows and dismiss are far below touch-target size; swap semantics differ from the drag mental model
findings.evidence: `.lm-recall-arrow-btn { font-size: 8px; padding: 2px 6px; line-height: 1 }` (lines 2834-2839) stacked with `gap: 2px` (2830-2833) gives two ~20x12px targets 2px apart, next to the 44px card tap zone that means 'select for swap' (ReorderRecall.jsx lines 94, 104-106). `.lm-recall-dismiss { font-size: 20px; padding: 0 4px }` (2695-2698) is ~18x20px. Tap-to-swap (lines 31-59) exchanges two positions rather than inserting, so moving item 4 to position 1 pushes item 1 down to 4, which the student then has to undo; a 4-item list is 3 swaps at most but the displacement is unintuitive. The instruction line (lines 79-81) is 11px italic dim text.
findings.studentImpact: On a phone the student either misses the tiny arrow and selects the card instead (purple ring appears, unclear why), or hits ▲ when aiming for ▼. Swapping instead of inserting leads to 'I moved it up and something else jumped to the bottom'.
findings.fix: Minimum 44x44 targets (`min-width/height: 44px`), one combined 'move up/down' control, or drop arrows and make tap-select then tap-position an insert (splice) not a swap. Make the instruction 13px and non-italic.

findings.title: FillIn drag-and-drop is dead code on every platform (chips are never draggable), so tap is the only path and it cannot target a blank
findings.evidence: `handleDragStartWord` (lines 18-22) is defined but never attached; word chips (lines 103-109) have only `onClick` and no `draggable` attribute; the `onDragOver/onDrop` on blanks (lines 84-85) are unreachable. `handleTapWord` (lines 33-41) always fills `placed.indexOf(null)` (the first empty blank), and `handleTapBlank` (lines 43-48) only clears. To change blank 1 after filling 1-3 the student must clear 1, then the next chip goes into 1 (works) but to swap two placed words they must clear both and re-tap in order. `.lm-word-chip { cursor: grab }` (globals.css 2784) advertises a drag that does not exist.
findings.studentImpact: Tap works on iOS/Android (the good news) but a student who tries to drag, as the cursor and the file header 'Drag-and-Drop Label Recall' promise, sees nothing happen. Correcting a mistake in an earlier blank is a clear-and-refill dance.
findings.fix: Delete the DnD handlers and cursor:grab; add 'select a blank, then tap a chip' (highlight the active blank) and tap-on-filled-blank returns the word to the bank; or implement pointer-event drag like DiagramLabelDrill.

findings.title: Three shipped components are never mounted: InteractiveDiagram, DiagramLabelDrill, RecallCheckpoint
findings.evidence: `import RecallCheckpoint from './learn-mode/RecallCheckpoint'` (line 11) has no `<RecallCheckpoint` render anywhere in components/ or app/ (grep). `InteractiveDiagram.jsx` (hover tooltips + colour-role legend) and `DiagramLabelDrill.jsx` (pointer-event label drag with `touch-action: none`, 35px tolerance) have zero importers. Only ReorderRecall, FillInRecall, InlineDiagram and processSvg (also used by DiagramsTab.jsx line 3) are live. InteractiveDiagram is mouse-only anyway (`onMouseMove/onMouseLeave`, lines 181-184), so it would add nothing on touch; DiagramLabelDrill is the only genuinely active diagram exercise in the codebase and is the one not shipped. Duplicate CSS from the dead checkpoint (`.lm-recall-header/.lm-recall-dismiss/.lm-recall-prompt` at 2606-2624 vs 2692-2706) is overridden by the later block.
findings.studentImpact: The only interaction a student gets with a diagram is 'tap to enlarge'. The label drill that would make diagrams active exists, tested with touch in mind, but nobody sees it.
findings.fix: Remove the RecallCheckpoint import and dead CSS; delete InteractiveDiagram (mouse-only); wire DiagramLabelDrill behind a 'Label this diagram' button on InlineDiagram for SVG diagrams that have `text.draggable` labels (audit how many do).

findings.title: 'Tap to enlarge' on a phone opens a modal no larger than the inline diagram; no zoom
findings.evidence: Inline SVG is `width:100%` (processSvg.js lines 57-59) and only capped at 442px from `@media (min-width: 768px)` (globals.css line 1854), so on a 375-430px phone the inline diagram already fills the card. The modal clones that SVG (InlineDiagram.jsx lines 20-30) into `.lm-diagram-modal { max-width: 90vw; padding: 24px }` (globals.css 5820-5826) with `svg { max-width: 90vw; max-height: 85vh }` (5870-5876). No pinch/zoom handling; the only interactions are the scenario switcher (lines 101-109) and close.
findings.studentImpact: Student taps a dense AD/AS diagram expecting to read small labels; the modal is the same size, darker, with a × in the corner. It reads as broken.
findings.fix: On viewports <768px render the modal SVG at a fixed larger width inside an overflow:auto container (2x with horizontal scroll), or use a pinch-zoom lib; hide the 'Tap to enlarge' hint when the modal would not be bigger.

findings.title: Wrong fill-in answers are overwritten by the correct word, so the student cannot see what they put
findings.evidence: `{checked && isWrong ? recall.answers[blankIdx] : word || …}` replaces the student's word in the red blank with the answer; the 'Correct answers' strip (lines 128-135) repeats the same answers without mapping to blanks. In the mismatch sections it renders `undefined` → empty red blank.
findings.studentImpact: After checking, the student sees a red box containing the right answer and has no record of their own mistake to reflect on.
findings.fix: Show `word` struck through with the correct answer beside it; drop the redundant answer strip.

strengths: ReorderRecall works on touch without any drag: tap-select then tap-swap with an on-screen instruction (ReorderRecall.jsx lines 79-81) and a real position-swap animation (lines 38-56, globals.css 2813-2821); no HTML5 DnD dependency.

FillInRecall's tap path is complete on iOS/Android: chip fills next blank, tapping a filled blank clears it, Check is disabled until every slot is filled (lines 33-48, 119); comparison is case-insensitive (line 52).
Per-item ✓/✗ feedback and a count ('2 of 4 in the right position') in both widgets, with correct answers revealed on failure.
Content coverage is broad and structurally clean: 272 of 413 sections carry a recall (131 reorder, 141 fill-in), 0 malformed `shuffled` arrays, 0 identity shuffles, every fill-in has hints.

processSvg is a sensible, idempotent quality pass (min 2px strokes, min 4px points, text moved on top with paint-order halos, responsive sizing) applied consistently by InlineDiagram and DiagramsTab; the enlarge modal clones the processed SVG so halos survive, uses a portal, fades, and closes on Escape and backdrop tap.
InlineDiagram's scenario switcher (multiple SVGs per diagram, e.g. 'AD/AS Equilibrium: Multiple Scenarios') is a lightweight, touch-friendly way to show shifts without hover.

DiagramLabelDrill, though unmounted, is the right pattern for touch: pointer events, `touch-action: none`, global pointermove/up listeners, SVG CTM coordinate mapping, distance tolerance and shake feedback.
walkthrough: Based on code reading plus the DB dump; not run in a browser. A student on a phone (dark theme by default, layout.js line 56) opens economics 'introductory-concepts', passes or skips the pre-test, and reads step 1: two sections of notes. At the bottom is a lavender 'Quick Recall — Fill in the Blanks' card with three sentence rows, each with a dashed blank, and three word chips beneath. They tap a chip; it drops into the first blank, whether or not that is the one they meant. They tap the other two; Check lights up. If they tapped 'Show hints' first, the blanks showed 'Pr____'-style prefixes, and with the chips visible it was a matching exercise. On check, right blanks go green, wrong ones go red and now display the correct word instead of theirs. If this step had only one section (54 of 237 steps do), they tap Next and the very same card, in the same state, is the first thing on the next screen. If instead it is a Reorder, they see four cards with 1-4 numbers, tiny stacked ▲▼ arrows on the right, and an 11px italic line saying tap one then tap another to swap. Tapping a card gives it a purple ring; tapping a second animates the two swapping places (not inserting), which is surprising when moving item 4 to the top. 'Show hint' says 'The first step is \"Ide...\"', which they match against the visible list. One Check: green/red per position, '2 of 4 in the right position', and a plain 'Correct order' list with no explanation; no retry. On some sections the prompt is 'Rank these motives from most commonly cited to least' and their defensible order is marked wrong. On the last step of a block they may see a 'Diagram' card: a static SVG with 'Tap to enlarge' under it; the enlarged modal is the same width as the inline one on a phone. For 24 of the 39 blocks tagged with a diagramRef, and every Business block, no diagram appears at all and nothing says one was intended. If the student hits the mayos-human-relations or interpreting-ped-values fill-in, they place two words, the third chip has vanished, Check never enables, and they eventually find the × in the corner; that × records nothing, and at the end the completion screen shows a recall score built only from the ones they chose to answer, some counted twice.

findings.title: Every subsection title is rendered twice, back-to-back (h2 then h3)
findings.evidence:
LearnModeTab.jsx:366-368 renders `

{sec.title}

` and immediately ``; NoteSection.jsx:11 then renders `

{section.title}

` from the same `section.title`. ContentTab.jsx:112 uses NoteSection alone (no h2), so the duplication is Learn-Mode-only. CSS: .lm-section-title 20px/800 on mobile (globals.css:1414), .rl-note-section-title 15px/600 (globals.css:811,999).
findings.studentImpact: On step 1 the student reads 'Economics as a Social Science' in 20px bold, then 2px below it 'Economics as a Social Science' again in 15px inside the card, for every subsection on every step. It reads as a rendering glitch and wastes ~45px per subsection.
findings.fix: Remove the `<h2>` at LearnModeTab.jsx:367 or pass a `hideTitle` prop into NoteSection and skip the h3 when set. Keep exactly one heading per subsection.

findings.title: One Learn Mode step is ~5,300-5,900px tall on a 390px phone (7.5-8.5 screens, 13-15 cards) with no progressive disclosure and the Next button only at the bottom
findings.evidence: LearnModeTab.jsx:343-402 renders, unconditionally and all at once: previous step's recall widget, then for each of 2 sections (h2 + NoteSection = title, KeyIdea, body [avg 890 chars incl. 1-2 FlowChains], RealExample [avg 275 chars], Misconception [avg 320], ExamMatters [avg 234]), then InlineDiagram, InlineQuiz, InlinePractice, ExplainItBack toggle, TakeawayCard, the current step's recall widget, then `.lm-nav` (line 434). Measured on the live economics__introductory-concepts.json with mobile CSS widths (body padding 14px @globals.css:1382, rail 36px+16px gap @1900-1905, .rl-note-section padding 24px @806-810 giving a ~257px text column): step 1 ≈ 5,350px / 14 cards / 12 glossary underlines; step 3 ≈ 5,940px / 15 cards; every step ≥ 7.5 phone screens. No `lm-reveal-btn`/`rl-section-enter` usage exists in LearnModeTab (grep: 0 hits), so nothing is deferred.
findings.studentImpact: The student lands on step 1 and sees a quiz widget, a huge title, a duplicated title, a green card, three paragraphs, a flow timeline, three more coloured cards ... and must scroll ~8 screens past two more coloured card stacks, a quiz, a practice question and a takeaway before the first 'Next' button appears. This matches the live data (75% never advance past step 0): from a phone the step has no visible end, so 'progress' is invisible.
findings.fix: Either (a) one subsection per step (halves height; flatSteps at LearnModeTab.jsx:48-60 pairs 2), or (b) collapse RealExample/Misconception/ExamMatters into a single tabbed or accordion strip per subsection with only KeyIdea + body open by default, and (c) add a sticky bottom bar with Next/progress on mobile so the exit is always visible.

findings.title: Recall widget of the PREVIOUS step is injected above the new step's content, pushing the reading ~310px down and making steps 2+ open on a quiz before any teaching
findings.evidence: LearnModeTab.jsx:353-360 renders `prevRecall` (ReorderRecall/FillInRecall) before `<div className="lm-content">`; line 397-403 renders the current section's recall after the takeaway. Live data: all 10 subsections in introductory-concepts carry a recall (alternating reorder/fillin), so every step from 2 onward starts with a purple 'Complete the chain' card (~312px on mobile) whose prompt text is #d4bfff (globals.css:2704) and whose item text is the only readable part in light theme.
findings.studentImpact: Step 2 opens with 'Complete the chain: Positive / Normative / ought to' before the student has seen the step title. Combined with the pre-test gate, the first three things a new user meets are tests, not teaching.
findings.fix: Render the spaced recall after the step's own content (or as a separate 'checkpoint' mini-step), keep at most one recall widget per step, and use the section title as the first visible element.

findings.title: No visual hierarchy: Key Idea, body, Real Example, Misconception, Exam Matters all share the same size, weight and card treatment; only hue changes
findings.evidence:
globals.css:817-955: .rl-key-idea, .rl-real-example, .rl-misconception, .rl-exam-matters are all `border:1px; border-radius:8px; padding:12px 16px` (10px 12px on mobile), all labels are `font-size:10px; font-weight:700; uppercase`, all body `

` are 14px/1.65. The only differentiators are hue (green #059669 vs teal #10b981 for Key Idea vs Real Example - near-identical) and Key Idea's 3px left border. Body paragraphs (.rl-body-p, line 830) are 13px on mobile and text-secondary, i.e. smaller and lighter than the three 'supporting' cards that follow them. The Takeaway (.rl-takeaway, line 958) is the most muted element on the step (label in --text-muted, grey card) despite being the summary. The block/chapter title is never rendered as a heading in the structured path (LearnModeTab grep: `blockTitle` only reaches ExplainItBackUpgraded at line 390).
findings.studentImpact: A student scanning on a phone cannot tell which of the 5 cards per subsection to read first or which one the exam rewards; the misconception (amber) is visually louder than the key idea; the chapter they are in is only revealed inside the collapsed 'Explain it back: The Nature of Economics' toggle at the bottom.
findings.fix: Make Key Idea the single dominant element (larger type, filled background); demote Real Example / Misconception / Exam Matters to a compact secondary style (no coloured fill, small icon + label, or a single 'Exam lens' strip); render `step.blockTitle` as the chapter eyebrow above the section title; give the Takeaway the strongest treatment on last-in-block steps.

findings.title: Glossary highlighting re-underlines the same term in every card and paragraph; tooltip is mouseover-only with no touch/keyboard path
findings.evidence: glossary-highlight.js:17 `alreadyMatched` is a per-call Set, and parseInlineMarkdown is called separately per keyIdea/paragraph/bullet/card/takeaway item (NoteSection, BodyRenderer, TakeawayCard), so 'first occurrence per string' becomes 'once per card'. Measured on step 1: 'ceteris paribus' is underlined 5 times, 12-19 dotted underlines per step. GlossaryTooltip.jsx:39-42 binds only `mouseover`/`mouseout` on document; the span is `cursor:help` with no tabindex/role/aria-describedby (glossary-highlight.js:45). Underline colour --green-50 rgba(5,150,105,.4) ≈ 1.65:1 on white.
findings.studentImpact: On a phone the dotted underlines are visual noise with no discoverable interaction; a tap fires a synthetic mouseover so a 280px fixed tooltip appears and stays until the next tap or scroll, with no way to open it by keyboard or screen reader. Not tooltip spam (single JS tooltip), but repeated underlines make body text look link-littered.
findings.fix: Track matched terms across the whole step (pass a shared Set through parseInlineMarkdown, or highlight once per NoteSection), make the span a `<button type=button>` or add `tabindex=0` + `aria-describedby`, add a click/touchstart toggle with tap-outside dismiss, and skip highlighting inside Key Idea / Takeaway to keep those clean.

findings.title: Light theme: card labels and recall prompt fail contrast; the reorder/fill-in prompt is effectively invisible
findings.evidence: Computed ratios against #ffffff (light --bg-primary, globals.css:16): .lm-recall-prompt / .lm-recall-hint hard-coded `#d4bfff` (globals.css:2704, 2734) = 1.65:1; .lm-recall-label `#a78bfa` (2700) = 2.72:1; .rl-misconception-label --rl-amber #f59e0b (938) = 2.15:1; .rl-real-example-label --rl-teal #10b981 (926) = 2.54:1; .rl-exam-matters-label --rl-blue #3b82f6 = 3.68:1; .rl-key-idea-label --rl-green #059669 = 3.77:1; .rl-takeaway-label --text-muted #9ca3af (962) = 2.54:1; .lm-explain-textarea::placeholder and .lm-recall-dismiss use --text-dim #d1d5db = 1.47:1. All labels are 10px bold uppercase (needs 4.5:1). No `[data-theme="light"]` overrides exist for .lm-recall-* (grep). Default theme is dark (app/layout.js:56) where the same colours pass (7-9:1), so this hits users who opt into light mode.
findings.studentImpact: A light-mode student sees the purple recall card with four items but cannot read the instruction 'Put these in the right order:' (lavender on white); every card label ('COMMON MISCONCEPTION', 'REAL EXAMPLE') is a faint pastel strip.
findings.fix: Define light-theme variants: `--rl-amber-text:#b45309`, `--rl-teal-text:#047857`, `--rl-blue-text:#1d4ed8`, `--rl-green-text:#047857`; replace hard-coded `#d4bfff`/`#a78bfa` with a `--recall-accent` token that is `#6d28d9` in light; raise label size to 11px; never use --text-dim for text.

findings.title: Interactive recall items are click-only <div>s; zero ARIA across the step widgets; no :focus-visible styling anywhere
findings.evidence: ReorderRecall.jsx:90-96 `<div className="lm-recall-item" onClick={() => handleTap(i)}>` with no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown; arrow buttons (105-106) have text '▲'/'▼' and no aria-label; dismiss buttons (ReorderRecall.jsx:75, FillInRecall.jsx:66) are `×` with only `title="Skip"`. `grep -c 'aria-|role='` = 0 in InlineQuiz, ReorderRecall, FillInRecall, InlinePractice, ExplainItBackUpgraded, GlossaryTooltip. globals.css contains 0 `:focus-visible` rules; .lm-recall-textarea:focus (2632) and .lm-explain-textarea:focus (2879) set `outline:none` and rely on a border-colour swap. Headings: h2 per subsection (LearnModeTab:367) -> h3 duplicate (NoteSection:11) -> h4 subheadings (BodyRenderer:19); no h1 and no heading for the chapter/block.
findings.studentImpact: Keyboard and switch users cannot select items in the reorder recall at all; screen-reader users hear 'multiplication sign, button' for Skip and 'black up-pointing triangle' for move-up; textareas lose the default focus ring.
findings.fix: Make recall items `<button type=button aria-pressed={selected}>`; add `aria-label="Move up"/"Move down"/"Skip this check"`; add `.lm-quiz-option:focus-visible, .lm-recall-item:focus-visible, .lm-nav-next:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-green); outline-offset: 2px }`; keep outline on textareas; fix heading order (chapter h2 > section h3 > subhead h4).

findings.title: Content HTML is injected unescaped; glossary definition is used as a String.replace template so `$1` / `$&` sequences would be interpreted
findings.evidence: parse-inline-markdown.js:8-15 only converts `**`/`*`; raw text goes straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in KeyIdea/RealExample/MisconceptionCard/ExamMattersCard/BodyRenderer/TakeawayCard without escaping `<`,`>`,`&`. Live dump: 44 text fields contain raw `<`/`>` (e.g. business__globalisation.json > types-of-trade-blocs: 'FTA < customs union < single market'; business__the-market.json > ped-and-revenue: '(PED > 1)'); all are followed by a space so browsers render them as text today, but `` would execute. glossary-highlight.js:45 `part.replace(regex, \`$1\`)` puts the escaped definition inside the replacement pattern: a definition containing `$1` becomes the matched term, and because `'` is escaped to `'` (line 39) a definition containing `$'` becomes `$&` = the matched term. Live glossary has one `$` case ('Absolute poverty': '$2.15/day'); `$2` with a single capture group is left literal by V8, so nothing is corrupted today.
findings.studentImpact: None visible today. Latent: a future definition like 'below $1 a day' would render 'below Demand a day'; a content string with '<b' or '<1x' style text would lose words on screen.
findings.fix: HTML-escape the raw text (`&`, `<`, `>`) at the top of parseInlineMarkdown before applying the bold/italic regexes; in glossary-highlight use a replacer function `(m) => \`${m}\`` instead of a template string, and escape `$` in escapedDef.

findings.title: .rl-note-section keeps 24px horizontal padding on mobile, leaving a ~257px text column (~175px inside FlowChain cards) on a 390px phone
findings.evidence: globals.css:806-810 `.rl-note-section { padding: 20px 24px; border-left: 4px }` has no override in the `@media (max-width:768px)` block at 997-1009 (only the inner cards drop to 10px 12px). Width chain at 390px: 390 - 28 (.tab-content-body 14px, line 1382) - 52 (.lm-stepper-rail 36px + 16px gap, lines 1900-1905) = 310px content; minus 48 padding + 5 border = 257px; key-idea card inner ≈ 229px (~33 chars/line at 14px); FlowChain: .rl-flow-chain padding 10px + 28px node + 10px gap + 24px card padding = ~175px for 12.5px titles (~28 chars/line).
findings.studentImpact: Card text wraps every 5-6 words and flow-timeline titles like 'Isolate the variable of interest' wrap to 2 lines, inflating step height and making the coloured-card stack feel even taller.
findings.fix: Add `.rl-note-section { padding: 14px 12px; }` and `.lm-stepper-step { gap: 10px }` / hide the rail on mobile (use the top progress bar instead); consider removing the outer .rl-note-section card on mobile entirely.

findings.title: FlowChain subtitle feature depends on an ' — ' separator that content almost never uses
findings.evidence: FlowChain.jsx:56 `step.split(' — ')` (space, em dash, space) to derive title/subtitle. Across all 43 live sections: 1,083 flow steps, only 4 contain ' — '. Also: `steps` is rendered as plain text (no parseInlineMarkdown), so `**bold**` in a flow step would show literal asterisks.
findings.studentImpact: None today (the subtitle simply never appears); if authors start writing '–' or ' - ' the split silently fails. Minor inconsistency: flow steps cannot carry bold or glossary terms while every other text field can.
findings.fix: Either document the ' — ' convention in the content skill or accept an explicit `{title, subtitle}` object; run flow titles through parseInlineMarkdown for consistency.

strengths: highlightGlossaryTerms is careful: sorts longest-first, HTML-escapes definitions, and re-splits on tags after every insertion so spans never land inside attribute values or break `<strong>`/`<em>` markup (verified: 0 nesting oddities across all 43 sections). Cost is ~4-17ms per step for 252 terms - not a performance concern.

Inline markdown is minimal and well-behaved on the live corpus: 0 unbalanced asterisks, 0 newlines in text fields, 0 `a*b` strings that the italic regex would mangle, 0 `<letter` sequences that a browser would parse as a tag.
GlossaryTooltip is a single JS-managed, viewport-clamped popup (not a per-span CSS ::after), so there is no overlap/stacking spam even with 19 terms on screen.
Quiz options (InlineQuiz.jsx:93) and all recall action buttons are real `<button>` elements; the note components are tiny pure functions that are easy to restyle without touching data.
Dark theme (the default, app/layout.js:56) has strong body contrast: --text-secondary #cdd4e6 on #0f1117 = 12.7:1; card labels 7-9:1.

Mobile media query (globals.css:997-1009) does reduce inner card padding, body font and flow-node size; `.tab-content-body` sets overflow-wrap/min-width:0 so nothing scrolls horizontally; `.lm-nav` buttons go full-width on mobile (1415-1417).

Real Example / Misconception / Exam Matters content is genuinely good (Bank of England Brexit model, NHS funding as normative) - the problem is the quantity and the uniform packaging, not the writing.
walkthrough: Step 1 of 'Introductory Concepts' on a 390px phone, dark theme, after the pre-test: a 36px green stepper node with '1' sits in a left rail; to its right 'Step 1 of 5' and a '⋯' menu. Then a 20px bold title 'Economics as a Social Science', and 2px under it a card with a green left bar whose first line is - again - 'Economics as a Social Science' at 15px. Inside the card: a green-tinted 'KEY IDEA' box (10px uppercase label, 2-3 lines of 14px text in a ~229px column); then three 13px grey paragraphs ('**Economics** is classified as a **social science**...') with 'ceteris paribus', 'demand', 'inflation' dotted-underlined; a 'Two Branches' subhead; a boxed vertical timeline (01 Microeconomics, arrow, 02 Macroeconomics, arrow, blue RESULT chip) that fades in as it scrolls into view; another paragraph; then a teal 'REAL EXAMPLE' card (Bank of England Brexit model, ~5 lines), an amber 'COMMON MISCONCEPTION' card (~6 lines), a blue 'EXAM MATTERS' card (~5 lines). That is ~2,050px - roughly three phone screens - for one subsection. The same 20px title / 15px duplicate / green / grey / timeline x2 / teal / amber / blue sequence repeats for 'Positive and Normative Economics' (~1,940px). Then a 'QUICK QUIZ' card with 4 lettered buttons, a collapsed 'Explain it back: The Nature of Economics' toggle (the only place the chapter name appears), a grey 'CHAPTER TAKEAWAY' card with 3 ticks, then a purple 'Put these in the right order' card with 4 tappable rows and ▲▼ arrows, and finally, ~5,350px / 7.6 screens down, a full-width green 'Next' button. Step 2 opens with the purple fill-in card from step 1 before its own title. In light mode the purple card's instruction text is lavender-on-white (1.65:1) and every card label is a pastel strip.

Learn Mode pre-test: student opens a section, sees "Quick pre-test" with 3 MCQs drawn at random from the section's 25-question static bank (PreTest.jsx:9-10), options always in stored order. They answer, see a score out of 3 and "your brain is now primed", then click Start learning. On each block's last step a "Quick quiz" card shows ONE MCQ (the first unused index in block.quizIndices, i.e. almost always quiz[0..4]); after picking, the explanation appears and a 4-second "How sure were you?" row pops up, which writes to localStorage and is never read again. Roughly half the time one of the 3 pre-test questions reappears verbatim as an inline quiz. On completion, the post-test re-shows the identical 3 questions in the identical option order. Smart Practice (/practice, linked from Home "Practice Questions", sidebar and the completion screen): pick a subject card, then a topic screen where every unit is collapsed showing "0 / N"; student expands units and taps chips (no question counts, mastery bars empty for anyone new or anonymous), hits Start Practice, and gets a fixed 20-question session (random 20 of unseen + overdue, not balanced per topic), one card at a time with Check answer / Next / Skip and keyboard shortcuts. Wrong answers say "This question will come back" but nothing comes back in-session. Summary shows accuracy ring and a "RETRIED" count that is just the number wrong. If they return within a day to the same topic after a good session they are told "No questions available for the selected topics". Across everything, 64% of correct answers sit at option B and 70% of correct answers are the longest option, so a pattern-spotting student outperforms the pre-test without knowing anything.
strengths: (Q1, definitive) No question is generated at runtime by an LLM. Every MCQ shown in PreTest, InlineQuiz, PostTest, QuickFireDrill, QuizTab, the /fun blackjack pool and Smart Practice comes from the static Supabase table section_quiz.data (app/api/practice/questions/route.js:21-25, app/api/sections/[id]/route.js:13). The only LLM call sites in app/ are app/api/chat/route.js, app/api/learn-mode/grade-explanation/route.js and app/api/written-practice/evaluate/route.js (grading/tutoring, not authoring). The bank is 769 questions across 43 sections, 4 options each, every one has an explanation (0 missing, only 4 under 60 chars).

Explanations are generally examiner-grade: they state the rule AND say why the distractors fail (e.g. introductory-concepts quiz[3] distinguishes 'movement TO the PPF' from 'shift OF the PPF'; quiz[8] justifies why tap water, a free bus ride and free education are not free goods). Several questions test genuine IAL discrimination points: PPF pivot (quiz[23]), capital vs financial capital (quiz[15]), store of value under inflation (quiz[5]), multiplier arithmetic (aggregate-demand quiz[2], [11]), ratio calculations (assessing-competitiveness quiz[0-3]).

lib/spaced-repetition.js is a clean, pure, testable SM-2: 1d -> 3d -> interval*ease, ease +0.1 correct / -0.2 wrong, clamped 1.3-3.0, wrong answer returns in 10 minutes. Interval progression for a steadily-correct card is ~1, 3, 8, 22, 64 days, which is sane for exam revision. buildQueue's 70/30 overdue/new split with backfill is sensible.

Progress persists for FREE logged-in users: /api/practice/progress POST has no premium gate (app/api/practice/progress/route.js:40-77) and PracticeEngine writes there for any isLoggedIn user (PracticeEngine.jsx:470-485). Anonymous users get a localStorage fallback (PracticeEngine.jsx:10-33). Smart Practice itself is fully free and uses the anon client, so no paywall friction on the engine.

Skip does not record a result (PracticeEngine.jsx:509-517), so a student is not penalised for bailing on a question they have not studied yet. Pre-test has a visible 'Skip pre-test' button (PreTest.jsx:120).

Quick Fire drill and the 1/3/7/14-day review schedule reuse the whole 25-question bank rather than the 4-5 questions Learn Mode surfaces inline, so the bank is not wasted for students who finish a section.

QuizTab shows best score from user_quiz_attempts and offers 'Ask Tutor to Explain' with the exact question, student answer and correct answer pre-filled (QuizTab.jsx:146-155): a good wrong-answer remediation path for premium users.

findings.title: 64% of correct answers are option B; options are never shuffled anywhere
findings.evidence: Across all 769 questions in the DB dump, correctIndex distribution is {1: 492 (64%), 2: 219 (28%), 0: 37 (4.8%), 3: 21 (2.7%)}. Per-section it is worse: business__resource-management 23/25 are B, economics__supply 21/25, economics__government-intervention 21/25, business__external-influences 21/25. Additionally the correct option is the longest option in 540/769 (70%). Not one renderer shuffles: QuestionCard.jsx:94 `question.options?.map((option, i) =>`, InlineQuiz.jsx:92, PreTest.jsx:88, PostTest.jsx:109, QuickFireDrill.jsx:176, QuizTab.jsx:122 all map options in stored order and compare against the stored correctIndex.
findings.studentImpact: A student who always picks B scores ~64% on the pre-test, inline quizzes, Quick Fire and Smart Practice without reading; a student who picks the longest option scores ~70%. Pre/post-test 'improvement' and the SM-2 ease values are measuring pattern-spotting, not knowledge. Students who notice this (and IAL students are drilled to spot MCQ patterns) lose trust in the assessment.
findings.fix: Shuffle options per render with a seeded permutation (seed = sectionId:questionIndex:userId or Date) and map the selected index back through the permutation before comparing to correctIndex; do this once in a shared helper used by all six renderers. Separately, run a one-off content pass to rebalance correctIndex across A-D and to shorten correct options / lengthen distractors so length is not a tell.

findings.title: Any key whose name starts with a-d (Ctrl, Alt, Arrow keys, Backspace, CapsLock) selects an answer
findings.evidence: `else if (e.key.toLowerCase() >= 'a' && e.key.toLowerCase() <= String.fromCharCode(96 + optCount)) idx = e.key.toLowerCase().charCodeAt(0) - 97;` compares the whole key NAME lexically. 'control' >= 'a' && 'control' <= 'd' is true, so pressing Ctrl selects option C; 'alt' and 'arrowdown'/'arrowup' select A; 'backspace' selects B; 'capslock' selects C. The handler runs on window (line 48) for any non-input target and the guard `idx < optCount` (line 29) does not help because idx is already 0-3.
findings.studentImpact: A student who presses Ctrl (e.g. Ctrl+Tab to switch tab) or an arrow key to scroll has an answer silently selected and the card moves to phase 1 ('Check answer' lit). If they then press Enter expecting to advance, the wrong answer is checked and recorded into SM-2.
findings.fix: Require `e.key.length === 1` before the letter comparison (and ignore events with ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey).

findings.title: Confidence is never collected in Smart Practice; Learn Mode's confidence prompt writes to a localStorage key nothing reads
findings.evidence: PracticeEngine.jsx:466-467: `// Compute next review (no confidence parameter)` / `const updated = computeNextReview(current, correct);`. QuestionCard.jsx has no confidence UI at all. lib/spaced-repetition.js:37-71 fully implements confidence modulation ('guessed' -> ease -0.05 net and interval x0.7; 'certain' wrong -> extra -0.1) and the DB column last_confidence exists, but every row is written null (PracticeEngine.jsx:483). InlineQuiz.jsx:110-118 DOES ask 'How sure were you?' (auto-dismissing after 4s, line 21) and stores it at `revvy_confidence_${subjectId}_${sectionId}` (line 60); grep across app/, components/, lib/ finds zero readers of 'revvy_confidence'. It is not passed to onResult (line 31 fires before confidence is chosen) and not sent to any API.
findings.studentImpact: Lucky guesses in Smart Practice are scheduled identically to confident knowledge, so a B-guesser (see the bias finding) accumulates 'mastered' (repetitions>=3) cards they cannot actually answer. In Learn Mode the student is interrupted by a 4-second confidence prompt whose answer changes nothing they will ever see, which reads as a pointless widget.
findings.fix: Either add a 3-button confidence row to QuestionCard after reveal and pass it to computeNextReview (the lib already supports it), or remove the InlineQuiz confidence prompt until it feeds scheduling. Do not ship a prompt whose data is discarded.

findings.title: 'This question will come back' is false within a session; 'RETRIED' stat counts questions that were never retried
findings.evidence: QuestionCard.jsx:116 shows `This question will come back — spaced repetition.` on every wrong answer. The queue is built once at session start (PracticeEngine.jsx:433 buildQueue(...)) and handleAnswer (454-505) only updates progressMap; nothing re-enqueues the item. A wrong answer sets nextReview = now + 10 min (spaced-repetition.js:64) which only matters if the student starts a NEW session after 10 minutes. SessionSummary.jsx:7 `const totalRetried = results.filter(r => !r.correct).length;` is labelled 'RETRIED' at line 49.
findings.studentImpact: A student who gets 6 wrong is told six times the question will come back, finishes the 20-question session without seeing any of them again, and then sees 'RETRIED 6' on the summary. The product promises a Leitner-style loop it does not deliver in the moment the student expects it.
findings.fix: Re-append wrong items to the end of the in-session queue (cap once per item), or change the copy to 'Scheduled for review in 10 minutes' and rename the summary stat to 'To review'.

findings.title: After a good session the same topic shows 'No questions available' with no explanation, reading as missing content
findings.evidence:
buildQueue skips every question whose nextReview is in the future (spaced-repetition.js:114-119 'Future reviews are skipped'). A correct first answer sets intervalDays = 1 (line 44). So a student who selects one 25-question topic, answers 20 correctly today, then returns tomorrow morning (<24h) gets a queue of the 5 unseen only; if they had answered all 25 correctly, queue is empty and PracticeEngine.jsx:611-619 renders `

No questions available for the selected topics.

` plus 'Back to Setup'. The topic chips on the setup screen carry no 'due' count or question count (TopicStep 213-234 shows only a mastery bar), so nothing warns them before Start.
findings.studentImpact: This is the most direct code-level cause of the 'doesn't cover all topics' complaint: a diligent student is told outright there are no questions for the topic they just studied. They cannot tell the difference between 'you're up to date' and 'the app has no content here'.
findings.fix: Distinguish states: if progress exists but nothing is due, show 'All N questions in these topics are scheduled for review; next due in Xh' with an 'Practise anyway (review early)' button that includes not-yet-due cards at low priority. Show per-chip counts: 'N questions, M due today'.

findings.title: Pre-test questions reappear as the block's inline quiz (~50% of sections) and the post-test is the identical 3 questions in identical order
findings.evidence: PreTest.jsx:9-10 picks 3 random questions from the full quiz array. LearnModeTab.jsx:106-108 picks each block's inline quiz as the first unused index in block.quizIndices; in the DB these indices are 0-4 for Units 1-2 (introductory-concepts blocks: [0],[1],[2,3],[4],none; meeting-customer-needs: [0],[1],[2],[3],[4],none). P(at least one of 3 random from 25 lands in {0..4}) = 1 - C(20,3)/C(25,3) ~ 50%. PostTest.jsx:23 `const questions = pretestData?.questions || []` re-renders the same 3 questions with the same options order (line 109) after the student has seen the correct answers highlighted (PreTest.jsx:90-91).
findings.studentImpact: Half of students see a pre-test question again a few minutes later as the 'Quick quiz' with the answer already revealed, and every student takes a post-test where remembering 'it was B' counts as improvement. The pre/post delta shown on the completion screen is not evidence of learning.
findings.fix: Exclude the union of all blocks' quizIndices from the pre-test pool; for the post-test, sample 3 DIFFERENT questions on the same sub-topics (or at least re-shuffle options) and label it honestly. Also fix the pre-test copy: 'Perfect — your brain is now primed' after 0/3 (PreTest.jsx:135) reads as sarcasm to a nervous student.

findings.title: Learn Mode only ever surfaces ~5 of each section's 25 questions; 20 are reachable only via paywalled Quiz tab, Quick Fire, or /practice
findings.evidence: block.quizIndices in the DB reference only indices 0-4 (introductory-concepts: The Nature of Economics>[0], Scarcity>[1], PPF>[2,3], Specialisation>[4], Economic Systems>none). LearnModeTab.jsx:107 takes the first unused of those, so a section with 5 blocks shows at most 4-5 inline MCQs. The 'Economic Systems' block has quizIndices null even though quiz[6] (command economy) and quiz[21] (free market) exist for it. Units 3-4 sections have no quizIndices at all and fall through to distributeItems (LearnModeTab.jsx:122; utils.js:9-23) which places quiz[0] and quiz[1] on the 2 steps. QuizTab preview is capped at 2 (QuizTab.jsx:15-16).
findings.studentImpact: A free student who completes Learn Mode has met ~5 MCQs (3 pre-test + 4-5 inline, overlapping) out of 25 written for the section, then hits a paywall on the Quiz tab after 2. They perceive the section as lightly assessed, while the very same 25 questions are free at /practice, which they may never find (it lives outside the section tabs).
findings.fix: Map every block to at least 2 quiz indices in the content pipeline (auto-assign unmapped questions by sub-topic keyword), and surface a 'Practise these 25 questions' CTA on the completion screen that pre-selects this section in Smart Practice (CompletionScreen already links /practice at line 133 but without preselecting).

findings.title: Near-duplicate and identical-stem questions within sections; two identical stems have different 'correct' answers
findings.evidence: Word-overlap scan finds 85 near-duplicate pairs across 23 of 43 sections. Exact-stem repeats: economics__measures-economic-performance quiz[0] and quiz[12] are both 'Which of the following is NOT included in the measurement of GDP?' with correct 'Transfer payments such as pensions' vs 'Unpaid housework and childcare'; economics__government-intervention quiz[5]/quiz[18] both 'Which of the following is an example of government failure?' (rent controls vs Prohibition); quiz[1]/quiz[10] both 'A maximum price set below the equilibrium will lead to'. introductory-concepts has three pairs: quiz[0]/[17] (normative statement), quiz[3]/[13] (outward PPF shift, same correct option text), quiz[7]/[20] (more capital goods -> future outward shift), quiz[9]/[19] (ceteris paribus). meeting-customer-needs: quiz[0]/[10] (define niche market), quiz[5]/[12] (market map purpose), quiz[9]/[15] (luxury watch niche). Cross-section exact repeats: 'Which ratio excludes inventory' in assessing-competitiveness[4] and managing-finance[3]; 'Crowding out is most likely to occur when' in macroeconomic-objectives[2] and role-state-macroeconomy[4]. Quick Fire drill shows all 25 in one sitting (QuickFireDrill.jsx:12-15).
findings.studentImpact: In Quick Fire and a single-topic Smart Practice session the student answers what feels like the same question 2-3 times, and in the GDP case the 'same' question has two different right answers, which reads as an error. The effective bank per section is closer to 18-20 distinct items than 25.
findings.fix: Dedupe pass in the content pipeline (Jaccard on stem >= 0.5 or identical correct-option text); rewrite the second of each pair to test a different angle (e.g. numerical, diagram-based, or an 'odd one out' on the evaluation point).

findings.title: Examiner review of 10 questions: evaluative command words forced into MCQ, hedged-option tells, and some contestable keys
findings.evidence: (1) meeting-customer-needs quiz[24] stem 'Evaluate the claim: Market orientation is always superior...' and quiz[22] 'To what extent is market research likely to guarantee...': 'Evaluate' and 'To what extent' are 12-20 mark IAL command words; as MCQs the only non-absolute option is correct. 177/769 questions (23%) have a distractor containing always/never/only/all/interchangeable, so 'pick the hedged one' works without knowledge. (2) quiz[7] 'Adding value is best defined as: Increasing the selling price above the cost of inputs' conflates raising price with adding value; Edexcel's definition is the difference between selling price and cost of bought-in inputs, which the explanation itself gives. (3) quiz[17] Instagram analytics on the brand's OWN followers keyed as 'Secondary quantitative': first-party analytics is arguably primary; a prepared student could defend either. (4) quiz[16] keys surveys as 'Primary quantitative' although surveys can be qualitative (explanation asserts 'Surveys generate numerical data'). (5) quiz[6] 'NOT a common base for segmentation -> Technological': explanation names four bases including geographic, which is not among the options; weak distractor set. (6) introductory-concepts quiz[7] 'most likely to result in': option B 'A movement along the PPF with no change in productive capacity' is literally true in the short run; only the 'and outward shift in the future' clause makes D better, so the key depends on the student guessing the intended time frame. (7) quiz[22] correct option 'Higher productivity but potential monotony' bundles benefit+drawback in one option, an odd MCQ construction. (8) quiz[6] 'In a command economy... Central government planning' and quiz[21] are definitional restatements with no discrimination. (9) managing-finance quiz[0] uses £ while quiz[15] uses $ with the same template; question style inconsistent. (10) Good: quiz[8] free good, quiz[15] capital, quiz[23] PPF pivot, aggregate-demand quiz[2]/[11] multiplier, assessing-competitiveness quiz[0-3] ratios are exam-faithful. Region check: 21 'UK', 3 'NHS', 3 'Bank of England', 3 'CMA' mentions; 1 'Korea', 0 HK/Singapore/Malaysia/Pakistan/Middle East.
findings.studentImpact: IAL students report 'odd wording' because stems borrow essay command words, several keys are debatable, and the hedged/absolute pattern lets them get questions right for the wrong reason. Contexts are UK-domestic (NHS, CMA, Bank of England) for an audience in HK/Singapore/Malaysia/Pakistan sitting a paper that uses international contexts.
findings.fix: Content rules for the pipeline: no 'Evaluate/Assess/To what extent' stems in MCQ; max one absolute-word distractor per question; every key must be defensible against the Edexcel IAL definition; use international or neutral contexts (Singapore MAS, HKMA, Bank Negara, generic 'central bank'); one currency convention per subject.

findings.title: Units 3-4 are a fraction of Units 1-2 (2 blocks, 4 sub-sections, 10 questions vs 5-8 blocks, 10-24 sub-sections, 25 questions)
findings.evidence: index.json: every WBS13/WBS14 section (10 of 20 business sections) and 9 of the 11 WEC13/WEC14 sections have blocks=2-4, subsections=4-8, quiz=10-14, reorder=0, fillin=0. Examples: business__business-objectives-strategy blocks=2 subs=4 quiz=10 (sub-sections: mission-and-objectives, swot-analysis, ansoffs-matrix, porters-generic-strategies); economics__trade-global-economy blocks=2 subs=4 quiz=14. Compare WBS11 managing-people blocks=6 subs=19 quiz=25 reorder=10 fillin=9. In Learn Mode a Unit 3/4 section is therefore 2 steps long with 2 inline MCQs and no recall widgets.
findings.studentImpact: A Year 13 student (the cohort revising WEC13/WEC14/WBS13/WBS14 for the summer exams) opens a section and finishes it in two steps with 2 quizzes, sees no reorder/fill-in activities they saw in Unit 1, and concludes the app 'doesn't cover' their year. This is the second concrete source of the 'doesn't cover all topics' complaint, and Smart Practice for a whole Unit 3 selection is at most ~60 questions.
findings.fix: Prioritise the content pipeline on Units 3-4 to Unit-1 depth (aim 25 questions, >=4 blocks, recalls). Until then, show honest depth signals: on the topic chips and section header display 'N questions' and a 'Coming soon: more content' badge instead of silently shipping 10.

findings.title: Session composition is random across selected topics; a 20-question session can be dominated by one topic
findings.evidence: buildQueue pools all unseen items from all selected sections into one array, `shuffle(unseen)` (line 127), takes the first `newTarget` (line 136) and shuffles again (line 141). There is no per-section stratification; with 6 topics selected x 25 unseen = 150 items, the 20 chosen are a random draw, so 0 from one topic and 6 from another is common. Session size is hard-coded to 20 (PracticeEngine.jsx:437) with no UI to change it.
findings.studentImpact: A student who deliberately picks 'the six topics I'm weakest on' gets a session that skips some of them entirely and has no way to request 'more' or 'fewer' questions.
findings.fix: Round-robin across selected sections when drawing unseen items (interleave by section, then shuffle within rounds), and expose a session length picker (10/20/40).

findings.title: Topic picker: all units collapsed by default, unit-number badge is the hidden select-all, chips show no question/due counts
findings.evidence: TopicStep initialises `expandedUnits = new Set()` (line 125) so on entry the student sees only unit rows each reading '0 / N' with a chevron. The select-all affordance is the small numbered badge (lines 192-194) whose only hint is a `title` tooltip ('Select all'), while the header text and right side both toggle expand (195-198). Chips render short_title plus a mastery bar only `if (prog && prog.total > 0)` (228), and mastery = repetitions >= 3 (progress-summary route.js:53), so every chip is blank for a new user; for anonymous users progress-summary never queries progress at all (route.js:41 `if (user)`), so the bars never appear even after sessions. No chip shows how many questions it has or how many are due. Subtitle copy 'Select the topics you want to be assessed on' (166) frames practice as assessment.
findings.studentImpact: A first-time student lands on a page that looks empty (every unit '0 / N'), does not discover unit select-all, and has no information to decide between topics. Anonymous students see zero feedback loop on the topic screen across visits. The framing 'assessed on' raises stakes for a low-stakes practice tool.
findings.fix: Expand the first unit (or the unit the student was last in) by default; replace the badge with an explicit checkbox; show 'N questions - M due' on each chip for everyone (question counts need no auth; compute due count from localStorage for anonymous users); reword to 'Pick the topics you want to practise'.

findings.title: Smart Practice serves all 25 questions free while the section Quiz tab paywalls the same bank after 2
findings.evidence: QuizTab.jsx:15-16 `PREVIEW_LIMIT = 2; displayQuestions = previewMode ? questions.slice(0, 2)` with a PaywallOverlay ('You've previewed 2 of N questions', line 171). /api/practice/questions uses createAnonClient (route.js:21) with no auth or plan check and returns the full section_quiz.data for any section list; /practice/page.js renders PracticeEngine for logged-out users too.
findings.studentImpact: A free student who hits the Quiz-tab paywall and then finds /practice sees the identical questions for free and infers the paywall is arbitrary; a student who does not find /practice believes they have access to 2 questions per section. Either way the gating story is incoherent.
findings.fix: Decide one policy: either make Quiz tab preview larger and point its paywall at premium-only value (explanations + Ask Tutor + attempt history), or gate /practice consistently. Whichever is chosen, link the two surfaces so students know where the full bank lives.

findings.title: QuizTab preview scores are computed over 2 questions but the CTA copy implies the student's score
findings.evidence: handleSubmit computes finalScore over displayQuestions (2 in preview) and does not save (line 51 skips preview); score label says 'You answered X of 2 questions correctly' then PaywallOverlay. Best score banner is hidden in preview (line 93). No 'Try Again' in preview (line 113).
findings.studentImpact: Minor: the free student gets a 2-question 'quiz', cannot retry, and has no score history, so the tab feels like a demo rather than a feature.
findings.fix: Fold into the gating decision above; at minimum allow retry in preview and show the best-of-2 to logged-in free users.

findings.title: Diagram SVGs render at 270px on phones: 500-unit viewBox text at 9-10px becomes ~5px on screen; 'enlarge' modal is only ~25% bigger and has no pinch-zoom
findings.evidence: .lm-interactive-svg-wrapper svg { width:100%; height:auto; max-width:270px } (globals.css:3378-3381) is the base rule for every width <768px (tablet bump to 442px only at :1854). Live diagrams are viewBox="0 0 500 350" with <text> font-size 9-10 (economics__measures-economic-performance.json > diagrams[0] 'CPI Basket of Goods' min font 10, diagrams[1] 'Types of Unemployment' 30 text nodes, min font 9). 270/500 = 0.54 scale -> 4.9-5.4px glyphs. processSvg.js:46-52 then adds paint-order stroke-width 4 halos (2px at that scale) around those glyphs. The modal (.lm-diagram-modal svg max-width:90vw, globals.css:5865-5877) gives 324-351px on a 360-390px phone; InlineDiagram.jsx DiagramModal has no pinch/zoom/pan handling, backdrop click closes.
findings.studentImpact: On any phone the inline economics diagram is a coloured blob with unreadable labels; 'Tap to enlarge' opens a modal that is barely larger, still unreadable, and cannot be zoomed. Diagrams are a core Economics exam skill and the founder already flags them as 'passive'; on mobile they are effectively absent.
findings.fix: On <768px set .lm-interactive-svg-wrapper svg { max-width:100% } (the card already constrains width), enforce a minimum SVG font-size in processSvg (e.g. scale text to >=14 viewBox units, or set font-size via CSS `svg text { font-size: max(12px, ...)}`), and make the modal a full-screen sheet with touch-action:pinch-zoom / a simple CSS transform zoom. Consider a landscape hint for wide diagrams.

findings.title: Glossary highlighting re-runs ~372 regex builds + HTML splits per paragraph on every LearnModeTab re-render (quiz tap, menu toggle, transition flag)
findings.evidence: highlightGlossaryTerms copies+sorts glossaryTerms (line 15), then for each of 372 terms builds a RegExp (26) and re-splits the whole HTML string (31). It is called from parseInlineMarkdown for every paragraph and bullet (components/notes/BodyRenderer.jsx:15,35) and from KeyIdea/RealExample/Misconception/ExamMatters, inside render with no memo. LearnModeTab.jsx re-renders on setScores (43-45, fired by every quiz/recall answer), setShowMoreMenu (145), setIsTransitioning/setNodePopped/setStepComplete (149-163). A 2-section step has ~20-30 highlighted strings -> ~8-11k regex+split operations per re-render. glossary_terms.json has 372 terms (avg definition 152 chars, injected as data-definition on each match).
findings.studentImpact: On a mid/low-end Android (typical in the target markets) tapping a quiz option, a confidence button or 'Next' triggers a visible stall because all note text is re-highlighted from scratch; scrolling jank after each interaction.
findings.fix: Pre-compile one alternation RegExp per glossary list (useMemo on glossaryTerms), and memoize parsed HTML per (text, glossaryTerms) with useMemo/React.memo on NoteSection/BodyRenderer. Or pre-highlight server-side once per section.

findings.title: Recall-card text uses hardcoded lavender (#d4bfff) with no light-theme override: ~1.4:1 contrast on white
findings.evidence: .lm-recall-prompt { color:#d4bfff } (2704-2706), .lm-recall-hint { color:#d4bfff } (2734), .lm-word-chip { color:#d4bfff; background:rgba(167,139,250,0.12) } (2780-2785), .lm-recall-label #a78bfa (2700). 13 occurrences of #d4bfff/#a78bfa in globals.css; grep for '[data-theme="light"] .lm-' returns nothing. Light theme --bg-primary/--bg-card are #ffffff (globals.css:16-17). Card bg is rgba(167,139,250,0.06) over white.
findings.studentImpact: Any student who toggles light mode (theme-toggle-btn exists in the mobile header) cannot read the recall question prompt or the word-bank chips in fill-in-the-blank; the exercise looks like empty pills.
findings.fix: Define --lm-purple-text / --lm-purple-bg tokens in both [data-theme] blocks (e.g. light: #5b21b6 text) and replace the 13 hardcoded values.

findings.title: Reorder arrow buttons are ~12x20px tap targets; dismiss (x), more (...) and hint buttons are also far below 44px
findings.evidence: .lm-recall-arrow-btn { font-size:8px; padding:2px 6px; line-height:1 } (2834-2839) -> ~12px tall, two stacked with 2px gap = 26px total. .lm-recall-dismiss { font-size:20px; padding:0 4px } (2695-2698) ~20x28px. .lm-more-btn width:28px height:24px (2001-2007). .lm-recall-hint-btn padding 7px 14px, 12px font (2735-2739) ~28px. .lm-fillin-blank padding 4px 10px (2765-2770) ~26px tall (this is the tap target to un-place a word). .lm-word-chip 6px 14px ~30px. .scenario-btn 6px 14px ~27px. .tab-face on mobile 8px 10px, 12px font (1379) ~30px. No mobile overrides for any of these.
findings.studentImpact: Students mis-tap the up/down arrows (hitting the row instead, which selects the item for a swap), accidentally dismiss recall cards, and cannot reliably remove a wrongly placed word from a blank. Every 'quick' recall becomes fiddly on a phone.
findings.fix: On <768px give .lm-recall-arrow-btn min 36x36 (or drop arrows on touch and rely on tap-to-swap), .lm-recall-dismiss/.lm-more-btn 40x40 with negative margin, chips/blanks min-height 40px, tab-face min-height 40px.

findings.title: Section API payload is 152 KB raw / ~39 KB gzip, fetched uncached on every section switch, and 40% of it is tabs Learn Mode never shows
findings.evidence: route.js:8-17 runs 8 Supabase queries and returns all of them (19-28) with NextResponse.json and no Cache-Control / revalidate export (dynamic route handler => uncached). Largest section economics__measures-economic-performance.json = 155,665 bytes raw, 38,661 gzip; breakdown content 66KB, notes 26KB, quiz 14KB, diagrams 9KB, flashcards 4KB, practice 4KB, extras 4KB, mistakes 2KB. StudyApp.jsx:447-463 does a bare fetch per activeSection change and setSectionData(null) first (453); no in-memory map, so returning to a section already viewed refetches. Shared first-load JS measured from .next/build-manifest.json rootMainFiles+polyfills: 555 KB raw / 167 KB gzip (framer-motion, @ai-sdk, supabase-js all in dependencies).
findings.studentImpact: On a school Wi-Fi share (~1-2 Mbps effective, 200-400 ms RTT) each section switch is a blank screen for roughly 1-2 s (8 DB round-trips server-side + 39 KB transfer), and the first visit is ~200+ KB compressed before Learn Mode can hydrate. Going back to a section already read pays the full cost again.
findings.fix: Add `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate` (content is already ISR'd for 1h on the page route) or export revalidate; keep a client-side Map of loaded sections; consider a ?fields=content,diagrams,quiz,practice variant for Learn Mode and lazy-load notes/flashcards/extras on tab open.

findings.title: Next/Back are at the very bottom of a long step and not sticky; on mobile 'Back' is stacked full-width ABOVE 'Next'
findings.evidence: @media (max-width:768px) .lm-nav { flex-wrap:wrap } .lm-nav-back,.lm-nav-next,.lm-nav-complete { width:100% } .lm-nav-spacer { display:none } (1415-1417). DOM order in LearnModeTab.jsx:435-448 is Back -> spacer -> Next, so wrapped they stack Back on top. .lm-nav is position:static at the end of .lm-stepper-content (2184-2188). A last-in-block step renders: spaced recall card + 2 NoteSections + InlineDiagram + InlineQuiz + InlinePractice + ExplainItBack + TakeawayCard + immediate recall (LearnModeTab.jsx:355-405) before the nav.
findings.studentImpact: A student scrolls through 6-8 screens of content and exercises, reaches the bottom, and the first big button is 'Back'. There is no persistent way to advance; 75% of logged-in starts never leave step 0.
findings.fix: Reverse order on mobile (Next first via flex-direction:column-reverse or order:), and/or add a compact sticky bottom bar (position:sticky; bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) with Back/Next and the step counter.

findings.title: Explain-It-Back textarea is 13px on mobile, which triggers iOS Safari's auto-zoom on focus
findings.evidence: @media (max-width:768px) .lm-explain-textarea { min-height:70px; font-size:13px } (3109). app/layout.js viewport = { width:'device-width', initialScale:1, viewportFit:'cover' } with no maximumScale (correct for a11y), so iOS zooms the page ~1.23x when a <16px input is focused and does not zoom back out on blur.
findings.studentImpact: Tapping the free-text explanation box on an iPhone zooms the whole page in; after typing the layout stays zoomed and the student has to pinch out to see the Next button and cards.
findings.fix: Set font-size:16px on .lm-explain-textarea and .lm-recall-textarea at all widths (visually reduce with transform if desired).

findings.title: Stepper rail consumes 52px of horizontal space on phones with no mobile override; note text column is ~230px wide at 360px
findings.evidence: .lm-stepper-step { display:flex; gap:16px } .lm-stepper-rail { width:36px } .lm-stepper-node { width:36px; height:36px } (1900-1913). No lm-stepper rule exists inside any @media block (awk over media blocks returned nothing). Column math at 360px: 360 - 28 (.tab-content-body 14px sides, :1382) - 52 = 280px; .rl-note-section keeps padding 20px 24px on mobile (806-810, no override in the 997 block) -> ~232px of text at 13px (.rl-body-p 13px at :1006). Inside .lm-recall-card (16px 20px) + .lm-recall-item (10px 12px) + num + arrows the reorder text column is ~150px for items up to 65 chars (measures-economic-performance recall data).
findings.studentImpact: Text wraps to ~30 characters per line, reorder items become 4-5 line blocks, and the whole step is 30-40% longer than it needs to be, all for a single number circle on the left.
findings.fix: On <768px hide the rail (or render the node inline in the counter row), set .lm-stepper-step { gap:0 }, and reduce .rl-note-section padding to 14px 14px and .lm-recall-card to 12px 14px.

findings.title: Only 4 of 9 tabs fit at 360-390px; the other 5 are hidden behind a 28px fade with no scroll affordance
findings.evidence: Tabs per subject = 9 (StudyApp.jsx:30-39 defines 10; :241 filters diagrams to economics and mistakes to business). Mobile .tab-bar { overflow-x:auto; scrollbar-width:none; mask-image fade to transparent over the last 28px } (1372-1378, base 424-434). .tab-face { padding:8px 10px; font-size:12px } + 14px icon + 6px gap: Home (icon only) ~34px, Learn ~75px, Notes ~72px, Diagrams ~98px, Practice ~90px = ~369px, so Flashcards/Quiz/Tutor/Extras are off-screen at 360-390px. Learn Mode IS reachable without scrolling (2nd tab).
findings.studentImpact: Learn is visible, which is fine, but students never discover Flashcards/Quiz/Tutor/Extras (the paid features) unless they happen to swipe the strip; the fade looks like the row simply ends at Practice.
findings.fix: Show a chevron/overflow indicator when scrollWidth > clientWidth, or move secondary tabs into a 'More' sheet on mobile; scroll the active tab into view on change.

findings.title: 'Next' is disabled for 350ms of pure timer before the step swaps; the step-exit/enter animations that would justify it are never applied
findings.evidence: navigateToStep (148-172): forward path sets isTransitioning, then setTimeout(..., 350) before onStepChange; buttons have disabled={isTransitioning} (437,441,445) and the keyboard handler is also blocked via the early return (149). The only visible feedback is the 36px node pulsing (lmStepDone 0.4s, globals.css:1918-1926). .lm-stepper-content.step-exit / .step-enter (globals.css:3328-3329) are defined but the class is never added anywhere in LearnModeTab.jsx (grep 'step-enter' in components returns only CSS).
findings.studentImpact: Each tap on Next feels laggy: the button greys, nothing happens for a third of a second, then content jumps. Combined with the glossary re-render cost this can approach 0.5s+ on a slow phone.
findings.fix: Swap immediately (or after ~120ms) and animate the incoming content with the existing lmStepEnter keyframe, or use the View Transitions API. Do not block input on the timer.

findings.title: Loading state on section switch shows 'Content for this section is being prepared.' — same copy as the empty state
findings.evidence: renderTab(): if (!sectionData) renders 'Loading content...' with subtitle 'Content for this section is being prepared.' (650-657). sectionData is set to null at the start of every fetch (453, 605) so this shows for the full round-trip on every section change. LearnModeTab's genuine empty state uses the identical subtitle (LearnModeTab.jsx:243).
findings.studentImpact: On a slow school network the student reads that the topic is not ready yet and leaves, when it is simply still downloading; there is no spinner or skeleton to signal progress.
findings.fix: Use a skeleton/progress indicator for loading, keep the previous section on screen until the new one arrives, and reserve the 'being prepared' copy for a confirmed-empty response.

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion handling in CSS: 20+ keyframes, staggered flow-chain reveals and blur transitions always run
findings.evidence: grep 'prefers-reduced-motion' across globals.css and components returns only AnimatedTabBar.jsx:21 (hover tilt). globals.css defines lmStepExit/Enter with filter:blur (3260-3268), lmCelebrate*, lmCorrectPulse, lmNodePop, lmShake, recallSwap (2817-2821), rlSectionReveal (978-981), new-badge-pulse infinite (3125), lmTimerPulse infinite (3357). FlowChain.jsx:4-39 animates every flow step with delay i*0.1s + 0.35s, arrows +0.15s, result spring; all elements start opacity:0 (initial='hidden').
findings.studentImpact: Motion-sensitive students get continuous pulsing badges and cascading fade-ins on every step; everyone else waits ~0.5-1s for a 5-6 step causal chain to fully appear each time it scrolls into view.
findings.fix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration:0.01ms !important; transition-duration:0.01ms !important } } and pass `reducedMotion='user'` to framer-motion's MotionConfig; cap FlowChain total stagger at ~300ms.

findings.title: First thing on every new step is the PREVIOUS step's recall card, before any content
findings.evidence: Spaced recall (prevRecall) is rendered before .lm-content (355-362); scrollToTop(true) runs at step change (159), so the viewport lands on the purple .lm-recall-card. 24 of 24 sections in measures-economic-performance have a recall (12 reorder, 12 fillin), so this happens on 15 of 16 steps. On a 360px phone the reorder card (5 items x 4-5 lines) fills the first screen.
findings.studentImpact: A student who pressed Next expecting the next topic is immediately quizzed on wording from the last card, on a full-screen purple exercise, with the section title pushed below the fold. Dismiss (x) is a 20px target.
findings.fix: Render the spaced recall collapsed (one-line header + 'Try it' expander) or place it after the first NoteSection; keep the section title at the top.

findings.title: Body text is 13px on mobile across notes, takeaways, recall items and fill-in steps; labels are 10-11px
findings.evidence: @media (max-width:768px) .rl-body-p { font-size:13px } .rl-takeaway-item 13px (1006-1007); .lm-recall-item-text 13px (2722), .lm-fillin-step 13px (2757-2761), .lm-fillin-blank 13px, .lm-word-chip 13px, .lm-recall-hint-text 11px (2827), .lm-card-label 11px, .lm-diagram-enlarge-hint 11px (5791-5799), rl-*-label 10px uppercase (817-825, 930-950). Desktop bumps to 15-15.5px (1861-1866, 1882-1887) but mobile goes down, not up.
findings.studentImpact: Long revision reading sessions on a phone at 13px/1.7 with a ~230px column; students zoom (no maximumScale, good) which then breaks the fixed header layout.
findings.fix: Use 15-16px body on mobile (drop the 13px override), 12px minimum for labels/hints.

findings.title: AnimatedTabBar instantiates 5 springs + 2 motion elements per tab (45 springs) on mobile where the effect is disabled anyway
findings.evidence: useSpring x5 per AnimatedTab (33-37) and motion.div/motion.button (75-101) are created unconditionally; isMobileRef only skips the .set() calls (41). .tab-glow is display:none on mobile (globals.css:1380) but the motion.div is still mounted. framer-motion is also pulled into the shared bundle for FlowChain.
findings.studentImpact: Extra JS and layout work on every render of the shell for zero visual benefit on phones; contributes to the 167 KB gzip shared bundle.
findings.fix: Render a plain <button> tab when matchMedia('(max-width:768px)') or reduced-motion matches; lazy-load framer-motion only for desktop.
