findings.title: Tab bar click handler is on a div with role=tab; the real <button> has tabIndex=-1
findings.evidence: onClick on the wrapper div (69), role='tab' aria-selected (71-72); motion.button has tabIndex={-1} (91) and no onClick. No onKeyDown on the wrapper.
findings.studentImpact: Tabs cannot be reached or activated with a keyboard/switch device; screen readers announce a tab that is not focusable.
findings.fix: Move onClick/role/aria-selected onto the button, remove tabIndex=-1, add arrow-key handling on the tablist.

findings.title: Quiz confidence row auto-dismisses after 4s and remediation slides in 1s after a wrong answer, causing layout shifts under the thumb
findings.evidence: useEffect timer 4000ms sets confidenceTimedOut (19-24) which unmounts .lm-confidence-row and mounts a one-line 'No worries' div (110-126); handleSelect schedules revealPhase 2 at 200ms then remediation at +800ms (33-39) inserting a second full MCQ block below.
findings.studentImpact: While the student is reading the explanation the layout jumps twice (row collapses, remediation appears), so the Next button or the next card moves out from under a planned tap.
findings.fix: Keep the confidence row height reserved or do not auto-dismiss; mount remediation with a fixed-height placeholder or place it after an explicit 'Try a similar one' button.

strengths: Topic pages are ISR-cached (export const revalidate = 3600 in app/economics/[unit]/[topic]/page.jsx:4) with generateStaticParams, and StudyApp's isInitial guard (StudyApp.jsx:448-451) avoids a duplicate client fetch on first load.
The section API runs all 8 Supabase reads in one Promise.all; the largest section compresses to ~39 KB gzip, which is manageable even on a weak connection.

Safe-area handling is correct: viewportFit 'cover' in app/layout.js, env(safe-area-inset-top) on .mobile-header (globals.css:383-384) and .main-content, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on .tab-content-body (1382), and .app-layout uses 100dvh (267).

Tab strip is horizontally scrollable with hidden scrollbar and an edge fade (globals.css:1372-1378); Learn Mode is the 2nd tab and always visible at 360px; hover tilt/glow is disabled on mobile and for prefers-reduced-motion via matchMedia (AnimatedTabBar.jsx:18-30).
Quiz options are full-width ~44px-tall buttons (globals.css:2125-2132) and Next/Back/Complete go full-width on mobile (1416) — the two most-used controls have adequate tap targets.

Reorder supports tap-to-select then tap-to-swap (ReorderRecall.jsx:31-59) and fill-in supports tap-to-place/tap-to-remove (FillInRecall.jsx:33-48), so both work on touch even though HTML5 drag events do not.

Scroll handling is rAF-throttled with rubber-band guards (StudyApp.jsx:505-530), scroll-to-top on step change is 'instant' with an iOS Safari fallback (468-500), and the keyboard hint is hidden on mobile (globals.css:1423).

Dark theme is the SSR default and is applied before hydration (layout.js data-theme='dark' + inline script), so there is no theme flash; most lm- cards use theme tokens and have explicit [data-theme='dark'] overrides (globals.css:2527-2586).
processSvg enforces minimum stroke widths, moves text on top and adds text halos (processSvg.js) — the right idea for legibility, it just needs the rendering scale fixed.
Diagram enlarge modal is portalled to body with a proper close button, Escape handling and aria-label (InlineDiagram.jsx:7-72).
walkthrough: A first-time student on a 375px iPhone opens /economics/unit-2/measures-economic-performance on school Wi-Fi. The browser pulls ~167 KB gzip of shared JS plus an HTML document that already embeds the full 152 KB section JSON (8 tables, only 4 of which Learn Mode uses) in the RSC payload and again as sr-only SEO text. A fixed 48px header appears, then a sticky title block and a horizontally scrolling tab strip showing Home · Learn · Notes · Diagrams · Practice; Flashcards/Quiz/Tutor/Extras are off-screen behind a small fade. Learn is active, so the pre-test gate shows 3 MCQs (good 44px options), with 'Check my answers' disabled until all three are picked and 'Skip pre-test' under it. Step 1 of 16 then renders: a 36px numbered circle eats 52px on the left, leaving a ~230px column of 13px text inside padded cards; causal flow chains fade in one node at a time. At the end of the block the diagram appears at 270px wide with ~5px labels and 'Tap to enlarge', which opens a modal only slightly larger that cannot be pinched. Below it: a quiz (fine), a practice question, the Explain-It-Back box (focusing it zooms the page on iOS because the textarea is 13px), the takeaway, a purple recall card with 12px-tall up/down arrows, and finally a full-width 'Back' button with 'Next' underneath it. Tapping Next greys the button for 350 ms while the tiny circle pulses, then the page jumps to the top of step 2 — where the first thing on screen is the previous step's recall exercise again, and every note paragraph is re-highlighted against 372 glossary terms on each subsequent tap. Switching to another section blanks the screen with 'Content for this section is being prepared.' until 8 fresh DB reads and ~39 KB gzip arrive.

findings.title: MCQ correct answer sits at option B 64% of the time; option A/D almost never
findings.evidence: Aggregating all 769 quiz items in the DB dump (sections/*.json quiz[].correctIndex): index0=37 (4.8%), index1=492 (64%), index2=219 (28%), index3=21 (2.7%). 14 sections are ≥70% option-B: business resource-management 92%, external-influences 84%, economics supply 84%, government-intervention 84%, entrepreneurs-leaders 80%, global-markets-expansion 80%, macroeconomic-objectives-policies 76%, managing-finance 76%, meeting-customer-needs 76%. expand-quiz-*.mjs appends `[...existing, ...newQuestions]` (line 2044-2049) with no distribution check; no validator anywhere inspects correctIndex; InlineQuiz/PreTest/PostTest/QuickFire render options in stored order.
findings.studentImpact: A student who always taps B scores ~64% on the pre-test, post-test and quick-fire drill and 'improves' without learning; students notice this pattern quickly and stop trusting the quiz as a measure. Also a strong tell that questions were machine-generated and never reviewed.
findings.fix: Shuffle options at render time (store correct option text, not index) in InlineQuiz/PreTest/PostTest/QuickFireDrill; add a validator rule: per-section correctIndex histogram must have no bucket >40% and every bucket ≥10%; one-off script to rotate existing banks.

findings.title: Four fill-in recalls are unsolvable: duplicate answers make the last blank unfillable
findings.evidence: `const availableWords = shuffledWords.filter(w => !placed.includes(w));` removes EVERY chip equal to a placed word. `Check answers` is `disabled={!allFilled}` (line 59 allFilled = placed.every(w => w !== null)). Recalls with duplicate answers in the live DB: business managing-people > mayos-human-relations answers ["Hawthorne","Hawthorne","Human Relations"]; business the-market > ped-and-revenue ["increase","increase","price"]; economics consumer-behaviour-demand > utility-and-utility-maximisation ["utility","utility","diminishes"]; economics consumer-behaviour-demand > interpreting-ped-values ["elastic","inelastic","inelastic"]. (business managing-people > herzbergs-two-factor-theory ["Hygiene","Motivators","hygiene"] survives only because the filter is case-sensitive, so the bank shows the same word twice.)
findings.studentImpact: Student places 'Hawthorne' in blank 1, the second 'Hawthorne' chip vanishes, blank 2 can never be filled, the Check button stays greyed out forever; the only way forward is the × dismiss. In 1.3.2 Consumer Behaviour (the second economics section) this happens twice.
findings.fix: Track chips by index (placed stores chip indices, not strings) so duplicates are independent; validator: answers must be unique case-insensitively within one recall, or rewrite the 5 recalls.

findings.title: ~20% of reorder recalls have no genuine order but are graded position-exact
findings.evidence: Grading is `items.map((item, i) => norm(item) === norm(correctOrder[i]))`, all-or-nothing per position. Of 131 reorders in the DB, at least 26 are lists/classifications/subjective rankings/parallel items rather than sequences. Examples (block section id > correctOrder): economics introductory-concepts > the-ppf-model [On the PPF curve | Inside the curve | Outside the curve | Slope of the PPF]; introductory-concepts > free-market-command-and-mixed [What to produce? | How to produce it? | For whom? | Market, command or mixed economy answers these]; measures-economic-performance > income-method [Wages reward labour | Rent rewards land | Interest rewards capital | Profit rewards enterprise]; measures > rpi-vs-cpi (four differences, prompt 'in logical order'); measures > human-development-index; economic-growth > costs-growth-environment [pollution | depletion | inequality | climate]; economic-growth > recovery-phase [Boom | Downturn | Recession | Recovery] (cyclic, any rotation valid); macroeconomic-objectives-policies > low-stable-inflation ('Order the reasoning for a 2% target'), > evaluating-supply-side ('by importance'), > market-based-supply-side ('most to least direct'); consumer-behaviour-demand > factors-influencing-ped ('most to least important'), > interpreting-xed-values, > using-elasticities-for-business-decisions; price-determination > how-markets-reach-equilibrium (demand slopes down | supply slopes up are parallel); aggregate-supply > ad-as-equilibrium (draw AD | draw SRAS parallel); business planning-raising-finance > choosing-appropriate-finance (prompt 'Match the finance source to the most appropriate use' — a matching task in a reorder UI); managing-people > management-vs-leadership ('Match the focus to the correct role'); entrepreneurs-leaders > non-financial-motives ('Rank these motives from most commonly cited to least', includes 'Achieving extreme personal wealth' under NON-financial); financial-planning > fixed-variable-costs, > factors-affecting-forecasts; managing-finance > external-causes-of-failure ('most gradual to most sudden'). 30 of 131 use the criterion-free prompt 'Put these in the right order:'.
findings.studentImpact: Student is told they are wrong for placing 'Rent rewards land' before 'Wages reward labour' or 'Inside the curve' before 'Outside the curve'. This is exactly the founder's user-feedback hypothesis and it is concentrated in introductory-concepts, the section with 192 starts and 167 stuck at step 0: 2 of its 5 reorders (PPF model, economic systems) are non-sequences and a third (social-science 'Observe → Build model → Apply ceteris paribus → Isolate variable') is contrived.
findings.fix: Restrict type:'reorder' to cause→effect chains and processes; convert the rest to a 'match' or 'classify' recall type or to MCQ. Validator: reject prompts without an explicit criterion ('Put these in the right order:'), reject prompts beginning Match/Classify/Rank/Order ... by importance, and flag correctOrder items that share a leading token (e.g. 'Management:' ×2, 'Leadership:' ×2).

findings.title: Unit 2 → Unit 3 cliff: half the steps, zero recall widgets, no pinned quiz/practice/diagram, denser text
findings.evidence: From the DB dump: Economics U1 = 5.8 blocks/section, 14.0 subsections/section, 84 recalls over 6 sections (~14/section), 25 MCQs/section, 139 words/subsection, quizIndices/practiceIndices/diagramRef pinned on most blocks. U2 = 5.5 blocks, 15.8 subsections, 95 recalls, 24.7 MCQs. U3 = 3.6 blocks, 7.2 subsections, 0 recalls, 10.4 MCQs, 155 words/subsection, no pins. U4 = 2.3 blocks, 4.7 subsections, 0 recalls, 11.7 MCQs, 193 words/subsection. Business U1/U2 = 5.4/4.6 blocks, 14.4/11.6 subsections, 57/36 recalls, 25 MCQs; Business U3/U4 = exactly 2 blocks × 2 subsections in every one of the 10 sections, 0 recalls, 9.8/10 MCQs. Every U3-4 script (e.g. labour-markets.mjs, business-growth-u3.mjs) omits recall, quizIndices, practiceIndices, diagramRef entirely, so LearnModeTab.jsx:86 `hasRefs` is false and the section falls to the 'Legacy fallback' distribution (lines 114-118). U3-4 Learn Mode also covers less than its own Notes tab: economics revenue-costs-profits Notes has 8 topics (incl. 'Short-Run Cost Curves', 'Long-Run Cost Curves', 'Alternative Objectives on a Diagram') while Learn Mode has 4 blocks. All 21 U3-4 sections were written in two commits on 2026-03-20 (1732 + 1153 lines; 7 business scripts are 114-116 lines each).
findings.studentImpact: A student finishing 2.3.6 (5 blocks, 17 subsections, 17 recalls, 4 pinned diagrams, 25-question bank) opens 3.3.1 and gets 4 blocks/8 subsections with no recall widgets, no inline diagram/quiz/practice at chapter ends, longer paragraphs, a 10-question bank where the pre-test (3 random) and post-test (same 3, PostTest.jsx:18-23) and quick-fire (all 10) overlap heavily. Unit 4 sections are 2-3 steps total. The product visibly downgrades exactly when the student reaches the harder, exam-year content.
findings.fix: Bring U3-4 to the U1-2 template: ≥4 blocks, 1 recall per subsection (chains only), 25 MCQs, pins per block; add a validator rule that fails a push when a section's blocks < 4 or recalls/subsection < 0.5 or quiz < 20; prioritise economics 3.3.1-3.3.3 and business 3.3.1-3.3.2 (most-traversed after U2).

findings.title: 24 of 39 diagramRef pins silently resolve to nothing; economic-growth and macro-policies lose every inline diagram
findings.evidence: Matching is title-substring only: `const t = (d.title||'').toLowerCase(); return t.includes(ref) || ref.includes(t);` (lines 97-104). Refs are written as slugs or renamed titles, so they never match: economics economic-growth refs 'ad-as-growth', 'output-gap-diagram', 'trade-cycle-diagram', 'ad-as-shifts', 'ad-as-growth-analysis' vs titles 'The Business (Trade) Cycle', 'Output Gap Diagram', 'PPF: Actual vs Potential Growth' (5/5 blocks unresolved); macroeconomic-objectives-policies 'fiscal-policy-ad', 'monetary-policy-transmission', 'supply-side-lras', 'phillips-curve' vs 'Fiscal Policy: AD/AS Impact', 'The Phillips Curve' (4/4 unresolved); aggregate-demand 'Aggregate Demand Curve' vs 'The AD Curve'; aggregate-supply 'AD/AS Shifts', 'Self-Correcting Mechanism'; market-failure 'Deadweight Loss'; government-intervention 'Indirect Tax' vs 'Tax to Correct Negative Externality'; price-determination 'Consumer Surplus', 'Indirect Tax', 'Subsidy'; national-income 2; measures 1. 21 of the 24 are in sections that DO have a suitable diagram. business the-market refs 'demand-curve', 'supply-curve', 'equilibrium-diagram' and business has no diagrams at all. Neither _upgrade-template.mjs validate() (lines 101-161) nor audit-diagrams.mjs (which only iterates 5 econ sections, lines 3-9) checks that a ref resolves.
findings.studentImpact: In 2.3.5 Economic Growth and 2.3.6 Macro Policies the student reads about output gaps, the trade cycle, fiscal/monetary transmission and the Phillips curve and never sees the diagram inline (InlineDiagram/DiagramLabelDrill never render), even though the SVG exists one tab away. Diagrams are the one active element in these sections.
findings.fix: Give diagrams an id and pin by id; run the same resolver in the validator before push; fix the 24 refs now (title strings) and fail the push on any unresolved ref.

findings.title: Validator only checks lengths/presence; half the content scripts have no validator at all; check-learn-content.mjs counts a field that no longer exists
findings.evidence: validate() checks: title present, sections non-empty, takeaway ≥3 and ≤100 chars, unique section id, keyIdea ≤180 and no '**', body non-empty, flow 2-4 steps and resultType enum, realExample/misconception/examMatters present. It never touches recall, quizIndices, practiceIndices, diagramRef, quiz, or practice. 21 of 43 upgrade-content-*.mjs scripts contain no validate() (introductory-concepts.mjs pushes CONTENT directly at lines 511-514; every U3-4 script; business meeting-customer-needs has validate but 0 recalls). check-learn-content.mjs:29 sums `s.concepts?.length` — the pre-March 'concepts[]' format that upgrade scripts explicitly replaced ('Rewrites section_content from old concepts[] format to new sections[] format', labour-markets.mjs:3) — so it prints '0 concepts' for every section and cannot detect anything. Concrete escapes: 80 fill-in hints whose underscore count ≠ answer length (e.g. 'independence'(12) vs 'in___________'(13), 'short-term'(10) vs 'sho______'(9)); 8 fill-ins whose template has more '___' than answers; 5 with duplicate answers; 2 duplicate MCQ questions (government-intervention quiz[5]==quiz[18], measures-economic-performance quiz[12]); business financial-planning quiz[3] options ['£500','-£1,500','£500','£10,500'] with correctIndex 0 so choosing the identical option C is marked wrong; 24 unresolved diagramRefs; option-B bias.
findings.studentImpact: Every one of the bugs above reached production because nothing between the author's editor and the live table could see them. The student meets them in the first two economics sections.
findings.fix: One shared validate() imported by every script (and run against the DB row after push), checking: reorder — 3-5 items, shuffled is a permutation, not identity, prompt states criterion; fillin — answers unique, blanks == answers, one blank per line, hint prefix and length match answer, no comma answers; quiz — 4 unique options, correctIndex in range, no duplicate stems, per-section correctIndex histogram, explanation references the correct option; pins — quizIndices/practiceIndices in range and not reused across blocks, diagramRef resolves with the runtime matcher; coverage — blocks ≥4, recalls/subsection ≥0.5, quiz ≥20, Learn Mode block titles ⊇ Notes titles. Delete or fix check-learn-content.mjs.

findings.title: practiceIndices are applied to the marks-sorted array, so the pinned practice question is not the one the author chose
findings.evidence: `const sortedPractice = useMemo(() => [...practiceData].sort((a,b) => a.marks - b.marks))` and line 110-112 indexes `sortedPractice[pi]`. _upgrade-template.mjs:43 documents practiceIndices as 'indices into the section's practice array'. upgrade-content-introductory-concepts.mjs:209 has `practiceIndices: [1], // PPF practice question` under the PPF block; seed/economics-practice-unit1.mjs practice[1] is 'Explain two reasons why the basic economic problem is relevant...' (6 marks) and the PPF question is practice[2] (10 marks). After sorting by marks [4,4,6,10,20], sortedPractice[1] = 'Outline two assumptions commonly made when constructing economic models' (4 marks). Block 5 `practiceIndices: [2] // economic systems practice question` (line 400) resolves to the basic-economic-problem 6-marker. Neither matches under either interpretation.
findings.studentImpact: At the end of the PPF chapter in the most-started section, the written practice question is about model assumptions, not the PPF the student just studied; the 'economic systems' chapter gets a question about scarcity. The practice feels randomly attached because it is.
findings.fix: Index into the unsorted practice array (or pin by a stable practice id) and add a validator that prints the resolved question text next to each pin so the author can eyeball it.

findings.title: Fill-in templates with 2+ blanks on one line are truncated on screen and need comma answers
findings.evidence: `const [before, after] = part.split('___');` keeps only the first two pieces of a template line, and blankIdx (line 72) assumes one blank per line. Live recalls that break this: economics introductory-concepts > money-and-exchange template '→ Money also serves as a store of ___, unit of ___, and standard of deferred payment' with answers ['wants','exchange','value, account'] — renders 'store of [blank], unit of ' and drops ', and standard of deferred payment'; aggregate-supply > changes-in-equilibrium 'AD shifts right → price level ___ and real GDP ___' answers ['rises, rises','rises, falls','stagflation'] — second blank disappears, chip reads 'rises, rises'; aggregate-supply > supply-side-shocks; business entrepreneurs-leaders > opportunity-cost 'value of the ___ ___ ___ forgone' (answer 'next best alternative', word 'forgone' dropped); managing-people > employer-employee-relationships ('___ ___ represent workers'), selection-methods, mayos-human-relations, leadership-styles ('___-___ leaders' → 'Laissez-faire'). 8 recalls total; 17 answers are multi-word or comma-joined.
findings.studentImpact: Student sees a sentence cut off mid-clause and a word-bank chip 'rises, rises' or 'value, account' that gives the structure away; drag-and-drop of a comma pair into a single blank reads as broken.
findings.fix: Validator: exactly one '___' per template line and answers must be single tokens (or support multiple blanks per line in the renderer); rewrite the 8 recalls.

findings.title: Only 6 shuffle permutations across 131 reorders; two of them cover 76%, so the fix pattern is memorisable
findings.evidence: `useState(() => recall.shuffled.map(i => recall.correctOrder[i]))` uses the hand-typed array verbatim. Across all upgrade scripts and the DB: [2,0,3,1] ×56, [3,1,0,2] ×43, [1,3,0,2] ×12, [3,0,2,1] ×11, [2,3,0,1] ×7, [1,2,0] ×2. 129 of 131 reorders have exactly 4 items.
findings.studentImpact: Every reorder in a section is displayed as [step3, step1, step4, step2] or [step4, step2, step1, step3]; after two or three the student solves it by pattern ('swap 1↔2, then 3↔4') rather than by recalling the chain, which also inflates recall scores fed to the completion screen.
findings.fix: Drop `shuffled` from content; Fisher-Yates at mount with a rejection rule (not identity, first item not already in place).

findings.title: Business has zero diagrams across all 19 sections; the Diagrams tab (a free tab) is empty and Business Learn Mode never shows a diagram
findings.evidence: index.json: every business section has diagrams: 0. business the-market blocks pin diagramRef 'demand-curve', 'supply-curve', 'equilibrium-diagram' (upgrade-content-business-the-market.mjs, 3 refs) to a table with no rows. audit-diagrams.mjs hard-codes 5 economics sections only. The economics diagram set already contains demand/supply/equilibrium/PED SVGs that WBS11 1.3.2 The Market needs.
findings.studentImpact: A Business student (half the catalogue) never gets InlineDiagram or DiagramLabelDrill; the Diagrams tab shows nothing; 1.3.2 The Market, 2.3.2 Financial Planning (break-even chart) and 3.3.3 Decision-Making (decision trees) are diagram-based exam topics with no visual.
findings.fix: Reuse economics demand/supply/equilibrium/elasticity SVGs for business the-market immediately; commission break-even, cash-flow, decision-tree, Boston Matrix, Ansoff, product life cycle SVGs; extend audit-diagrams.mjs to both subjects and fail on empty.

findings.title: No item ids, no versioning, no review step: pushes are blind full overwrites of live data
findings.evidence: `supabase.from('section_content').update({ data: CONTENT }).eq('section_id', section.id)` replaces the whole JSON with the in-memory constant; no backup read, no version/updated_at column in seed/business-schema.sql, no diff printed. Quiz, practice and diagram items in the dump have no id (diagram.id is undefined; quiz keys are question/options/correctIndex/explanation), so blocks pin by array position (quizIndices/practiceIndices) and LearnModeTab.jsx:107/111 silently skips an index that is out of range or already used — a block just loses its quiz with no error. Dedupe of the duplicate government-intervention quiz[5]/[18] or any reorder of a bank would shift pins. The only history is git on the scripts (43 scripts share one mtime, 2026-03-20 09:xx, i.e. checkout time), and scripts are committed after the DB was already updated with a service-role key (_db.mjs). The author's intent lives only in code comments ('// PPF practice question').
findings.studentImpact: A bad push (or the practiceIndices bug above) goes live instantly for all 211 users with nothing to roll back to; when content is fixed later, pins drift and chapter-end quizzes/practice quietly vanish.
findings.fix: Add id to every quiz/practice/diagram item and pin by id; store content_version + previous JSON (or a section_content_history table) on every update; make the push script print a resolved-pins report and a diff and require a --confirm flag; add a staging section_id or a draft column reviewed in the admin UI before publish.

findings.title: Content was bulk-generated from a template and is UK-centric for an international IAL audience
findings.evidence: Uniformity: every subsection has the identical 6 parts + emoji; 129/131 reorders have exactly 4 items and 141/141 fill-ins exactly 3 answers; 30 reorder prompts are the literal 'Put these in the right order:' and 49 fill-in prompts the literal 'Complete the chain:'; 6 shuffle permutations; hints with wrong underscore counts 80 times; option-B bias 64%. Velocity: 5 sections / 3283 lines in one commit at 09:07 (2026-03-18), recall widgets for 3 sections (359 lines) 2.5 h later, 21 U3-4 sections in two commits on 2026-03-20, 7 business scripts each 114-116 lines. Audience fit: 272 UK/£/NHS/ONS/Bank of England mentions in content vs 49 mentions of HK/SG/MY/PK/LK/KR/Gulf; 132 of 413 realExamples are UK-flavoured vs 24 targeting the stated markets; introductory-concepts > economics-as-a-social-science realExample is 'Bank of England ... Brexit', practice guidance cites NHS/ONS; measures-economic-performance > rpi-vs-cpi drills a UK-only statistic ('council tax') that WEC12 does not require.
findings.studentImpact: A student in Lahore or Hong Kong reads Brexit, NHS and council-tax examples in a course that is sold as IAL-specific; the sameness of prompts and shapes reads as filler, and the founder's 'question wording is odd' feedback follows from unedited generation.
findings.fix: Keep generation but add a human edit pass per section with a checklist (criterion in every prompt, example relevant to IAL markets, RPI/UK-only content removed), and make the validator enforce the mechanical parts so the human pass can focus on meaning.

findings.title: Practice question text embeds '(N marks)' while InlinePractice also renders an 'N marks' badge
findings.evidence: 165 practice questions in the dump end with '(4 marks)'/'(6 marks)' etc. (seed/economics-practice-unit1.mjs: "Define the term 'opportunity cost'. (4 marks)" with a separate marks: 4 field); InlinePractice renders `{question.marks} marks` in a badge next to the text, and the AI-marking prompt (line 19) repeats it a third time.
findings.studentImpact: 'Define the term opportunity cost. (4 marks)  [4 marks]' — small, but it is the first written question a student sees and it looks unedited.
findings.fix: Strip the trailing '(N marks)' in the seed (one regex) and rely on the marks field.

strengths: The structured schema (keyIdea → body → realExample → misconception → examMatters → takeaway, with flow chains) is pedagogically sound and consistently applied; the writing rules in _upgrade-template.mjs:7-15 (180-char keyIdea, 3-sentence misconception 'wrong → why → what to write', named-entity examples) are specific and good.
validate() in the template does catch real, push-blocking errors (duplicate section ids, bold in keyIdea, flow step limits) and exits before touching the DB (lines 165-174).

Most Unit 1-2 economics reorders that ARE sequences are genuinely good cause→effect chains (e.g. government-intervention > how-indirect-taxes-correct-market-failure, how-maximum-prices-work; national-income > adjustment-to-equilibrium; market-failure > characteristics-public-goods); market-failure recalls are almost all real chains.
ReorderRecall's norm() (trim, quote/dash/whitespace normalisation) and FillInRecall's case-insensitive check are robust against content typos.
Block-level pinning (quizIndices/practiceIndices/diagramRef) is the right design; it just needs ids and a resolver in the validator.

Practice guidance is mark-by-mark and command-word aligned (Define/Explain/Assess/Evaluate/Outline), mirroring IAL paper structure; every MCQ has an explanation that says why the distractors are wrong.
Scripts are in git with a readable commit history, so the pipeline is auditable even though the DB itself is not versioned.
walkthrough: A new economics student opens 1.3.1 Introductory Concepts. Pre-test: 3 MCQs drawn from a bank where the right answer is B two-thirds of the time. Step 1 reads well (keyIdea, bolded terms, a Bank of England/Brexit example). At the bottom, a reorder asks to 'Put these in the right order:' Observe behaviour → Build model → Apply ceteris paribus → Isolate variable — a contrived sequence, displayed in the same [3,1,4,2] shuffle every other reorder will use. Step 3 (PPF) ends with a reorder of 'On the curve / Inside / Outside / Slope' that has no order, and the chapter's pinned written question turns out to be 'Outline two assumptions of economic models' rather than the PPF question the author intended, because indices are applied to a marks-sorted array. Step 4's fill-in on money truncates the sentence after 'unit of' and offers a chip reading 'value, account'. In 1.3.2 the student hits two fill-ins that cannot be completed at all (duplicate 'utility' / 'inelastic' chips vanish from the bank) and must click × to move on. In 2.3.5/2.3.6 every chapter-end diagram fails to resolve, so output gaps, the trade cycle and the Phillips curve are text only. Reaching Unit 3, the section shrinks to 3-4 blocks, every recall widget disappears, nothing is pinned, the quiz bank drops to 10 and the post-test re-asks the same 3 pre-test questions. A Business student never sees a diagram anywhere. None of this was catchable by the current tooling: the template validator checks string lengths, half the scripts skip it, and check-learn-content.mjs counts a field that no longer exists.
